content.text: I want an implementation of openchoreo running in my lab. It should be deployed via fleet and have its own namespace and fleet app bundle
I'll start by understanding the repo's conventions for fleet bundles, then look at what OpenChoreo needs.

1 # lab-fleet — Home Lab Cluster Configuration as Code 2 [![FOSSA Status](https://app.fossa.com/api/projects/git%2Bgithub.com%2Fdarthzen%2Flab-fleet.svg?type=shield)](https://app.fossa.com/projects/git%2Bgithub.com%2Fdarthzen%2Flab-fleet?ref=badge_shield) 3 4 5 The complete, install-ordered configuration of a single-node k3s cluster running a private AI platform: local LLM inference on a Tesla V100, RAG over Milvus, agentic MCP tooling, GPU image generation, and the home services that share the node. Every file was curated from **live cluster state** — helm values pulled from running releases, manifests reconstructed from applied objects, and application sources recovered from container image layers after their Dockerfiles were lost. 6 7 This repo is mounted as the [`lab/` submodule of ash4d.com](https://github.com/darthzen/ash4d.com), which carries the full architecture documentation. This repo carries the configs. 8 9 ## Installation Order 10 11 ```mermaid 12 flowchart TD 13 subgraph host["00 — Host (openSUSE Leap 16.0)"] 14 DRIVER[NVIDIA G06 driver + CDI] 15 K3S[k3s v1.35] 16 end 17 18 subgraph platform["01-03 — Platform"] 19 METALLB[01 MetalLB
+ Traefik] 20 LONGHORN[02 Longhorn] 21 GPU[03 RuntimeClass
+ Device Plugin + DCGM] 22 end 23 24 subgraph ai["04-09 — AI Stack (namespace: ai)"] 25 OLLAMA[04 Ollama
Qwen3 / V100
+ exporter/proxy] 26 OWUI[05 Open WebUI] 27 MILVUS[06 Milvus + Attu] 28 COMFY[07 ComfyUI] 29 INDEXER[08 Doc indexers
k8s · suse · logicpro] 30 MCP[09 MCP layer
mcpo · k8s · github · docs-rag] 31 end 32 33 subgraph apps["10-13 — Applications"] 34 HERMES[10 Hermes Agent] 35 EMBY[11 Emby] 36 NODERED[12 Node-RED] 37 RESILIO[13 Resilio Sync] 38 end 39 40 subgraph mgmt["14 — Management Plane"] 41 RANCHER[Rancher downstream
Fleet · Monitoring] 42 end 43 44 subgraph pki["15 — PKI"] 45 CERTMGR[15 cert-manager
letsencrypt-dns DNS-01] 46 end 47 48 subgraph more["16-21 — Applications"] 49 ORIGIN[16 ash4d.com origin] 50 BUZZ[17 Buzz relay
+ MinIO] 51 MEMORY[18 lab-memory
Karakeep + MCP] 52 NEMO[19 NemoClaw
RBAC · netpol] 53 OPENSHELL[20 OpenShell
agent gateway] 54 UNSLOTH[21 Unsloth Studio
fine-tuning GUI / V100] 55 end 56 57 host --> platform --> ai --> apps 58 platform --> mgmt 59 platform --> pki 60 pki --> more 61 NEMO --> OPENSHELL 62 63 classDef ai_c fill:#059669,stroke:#047857,color:#fff 64 class OLLAMA,OWUI,MILVUS,COMFY,INDEXER,MCP,HERMES,UNSLOTH ai_c 65 ``` 66 67 ## Node Specifications 68 69 | Resource | Details | 70 |---|---| 71 | **Node** | Single-node k3s (`sdf1`) on openSUSE Leap 16.0 | 72 | **k3s Version** | v1.35.5+k3s1 (containerd 2.2.3-k3s1) | 73 | **GPU 0** | NVIDIA Tesla V100 32GB — LLM inference, pinned by UUID to Ollama; also ComfyUI's pin, which is why ComfyUI sits at `replicas: 0` | 74 | **GPU 1** | NVIDIA GTX 1070 8GB — Emby transcode (UUID pin) | 75 | **Load Balancer Pool** | MetalLB L2, `192.168.7.150-169` | 76 | **Storage** | Longhorn CSI across all stateful workloads | 77 78 ## Components 79 80 | Step | Component | Chart / Source | Version | 81 |---|---|---|---| 82 | 00 | Host prep (NVIDIA G06, CDI, k3s) | zypper / get.k3s.io | k3s v1.35.5+k3s1 | 83 | 01 | MetalLB + Traefik | metallb/metallb; k3s-bundled traefik | 0.16.1 / 39.0.7 (v3.6.12) | 84 | 02 | Longhorn | longhorn/longhorn | 1.12.0 | 85 | 03 | GPU (RuntimeClass, device plugin, DCGM) | nvdp/nvidia-device-plugin | 0.19.2 / dcgm 4.8.2 | 86 | 04 | Ollama (+ metrics/proxy exporter) | otwld ollama-helm | chart 1.67.0 (app 0.32.0) | 87 | 05 | Open WebUI | open-webui/open-webui | chart 14.8.0 (app 0.9.6) | 88 | 06 | Milvus (+ Attu UI) | zilliztech/milvus | chart 5.0.22 (app 2.6.18) | 89 | 07 | ComfyUI (+ filebrowser) — scaled to 0 | mmartial/comfyui-nvidia-docker | ubuntu22_cuda12.4.1-latest | 90 | 08 | Doc indexers (k8s, SUSE, Logic Pro) | local image + ConfigMap scripts | v2 | 91 | 09 | MCP layer (mcpo, k8s/github MCP, docs-rag MCP) | manifests + in-repo source | — | 92 | 10 | Hermes agent (Slack AI agent) | nousresearch/hermes-agent | latest | 93 | 11 | Emby media server (GPU transcode) | emby/embyserver | latest | 94 | 12 | Node-RED home automation | nodered/node-red | latest | 95 | 13 | Resilio Sync (P2P file sync) | resilio/sync | latest | 96 | 14 | Cluster mgmt plane (Rancher downstream + Fleet) | README only | v2.14.3 | 97 | 15 | cert-manager + `letsencrypt-dns` ClusterIssuer | jetstack/cert-manager | v1.20.2 | 98 | 16 | ash4d.com origin (nginx placeholder) | raw manifests | nginx-unprivileged:alpine | 99 | 17 | Buzz relay (+ standalone MinIO) | oci://ghcr.io/block/buzz/charts/buzz | 0.1.6 (app 0.1.0) | 100 | 18 | lab-memory — Karakeep + 3 MCP servers + ingest | karakeep-app/karakeep | chart 0.32.0 | 101 | 19 | NemoClaw ops-agent scaffolding (RBAC/netpol) | raw manifests | — | 102 | 20 | OpenShell agent gateway | **vendored** chart `helm-chart` | 0.0.0-dev | 103 | 21 | Unsloth Studio (fine-tuning GUI) — scaled to 0 | unsloth/unsloth | 2026.5.9 (studio v0.1.43-beta) | 104 105 ### Directory numbers 15+ are append-order, not install-order 106 107 `15`–`20` were added after the original `00`–`14` tree and are numbered in the 108 order they were adopted, not their true position in a dependency graph. 109 **cert-manager (15) actually installs before almost everything** — it issues the 110 TLS for `attu` (06), `hermes` (10), `lab-memory` (18) and `registry`, so on a 111 rebuild it belongs alongside `01`–`03`. It was appended rather than inserted 112 because renumbering the existing tree would invalidate every Fleet `GitRepo` 113 path and every cross-reference in the docs, for a cosmetic gain. 114 115 Real dependency order for the new components: 116 117 15-cert-manager → 16, 17, 18, 21 (anything terminating TLS in-cluster) 118 19-nemoclaw → 20-openshell (openshell writes into nemoclaw-sandboxes) 119 120 One chart, OpenShell (20), is **vendored** (committed under `20-openshell/chart/`) 121 rather than pulled from a repo — a departure from `04`/`05`/`06`. The running 122 release came from upstream's floating `0.0.0-dev` tag, and none of the published 123 immutable semvers (`0.0.37`–`0.0.42`) reproduces it, so the copy recovered from 124 the live Helm release Secret is the only artifact known to match the cluster. 125 126 Buzz (17) was briefly vendored too, on a wrong conclusion that its chart was 127 unpublished; it is now referenced upstream at an immutable `0.1.6`. See 128 `14-cluster-mgmt/FLEET-WIRING.md` for both stories. 129 130 Each directory contains a README with the exact install commands and the reasoning behind non-default values. Helm components follow one pattern: 131 132 ```bash 133 helm upgrade --install -n --create-namespace -f /values.yaml 134 ``` 135 136 ## How This Repo Was Built 137 138 ```mermaid 139 flowchart LR 140 CLUSTER[("Live k3s cluster
(source of truth)")] 141 DUMP[dump-lab-state.sh
helm values + manifests] 142 FORENSICS[recover-image-sources.sh
OCI layer forensics] 143 CURATE[Curation
clean · sanitize · document] 144 REPO[("lab-fleet")] 145 146 CLUSTER --> DUMP --> CURATE 147 CLUSTER --> FORENSICS --> CURATE 148 CURATE --> REPO 149 150 classDef tool fill:#059669,stroke:#047857,color:#fff 151 class DUMP,FORENSICS tool 152 ``` 153 154 Configuration was captured from the running cluster rather than from build-time notes, so it reflects what actually works — including fixes discovered in production (see the emptyDir EBUSY note in `08-indexer/`). The two locally-built images had lost their Dockerfiles entirely; their sources and build recipes were recovered by mounting the image snapshots and reconstructing build history from OCI layer metadata. 155 156 **Sanitization:** no kubeconfigs, tokens, or secret values live in this repo. Secrets are referenced via `secretKeyRef` with documented `kubectl create secret` commands and `.example` templates. 157 158 ## Related Repositories 159 160 - [`ash4d.com`](https://github.com/darthzen/ash4d.com) — architecture documentation, deployment plan, and public site; this repo is its `lab/` submodule 161 - [`ollama-code-mcp`](https://github.com/darthzen/ollama-code-mcp) — MCP server delegating Claude Code tasks to the Ollama instance defined here 162 163 ## About 164 165 Built by [Rick Ashford](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rickashford/) — Sales Engineering leader with 17 years at SUSE, specializing in Kubernetes, Linux, AI/LLM platforms, and open-source ecosystem strategy. 166 167 168 ## License 169 [![FOSSA Status](https://app.fossa.com/api/projects/git%2Bgithub.com%2Fdarthzen%2Flab-fleet.svg?type=large)](https://app.fossa.com/projects/git%2Bgithub.com%2Fdarthzen%2Flab-fleet?ref=badge_large)

=== 21-unsloth-studio/fleet.yaml ===
# Fleet bundle — Unsloth Studio, web GUI for LLM fine-tuning (raw manifest).
# GPU-pinned to the V100 by UUID via runtimeClassName: nvidia (NOT the device
# plugin), and declared at replicas: 0 — ollama holds the same V100 with
# OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1, so scale-up is a deliberate act (see README.md).
# Prerequisites before enabling this path: the unsloth-jupyter Secret must
# exist in ai (see README.md), and cert-manager + letsencrypt-dns must be live
# (Ingress hosts unsloth.ash4d.com and jupyter.ash4d.com).
defaultNamespace: ai

# Raw-manifest bundle, but Fleet still deploys it via Helm internally — so
# adopting the objects that are already on the cluster needs takeOwnership.
# Without it the first sync fails: the live objects carry no
# meta.helm.sh/release-name annotation, and Helm refuses to touch resources it
# does not believe it owns. With it, adoption is metadata-only (Helm labels on
# the top-level objects), so no pod template changes and no restarts.
# (This bundle is a fresh install with no pre-existing live objects, so
# takeOwnership is a no-op on first sync — kept for convention consistency and
# to protect a future re-adopt after a manual `kubectl apply`.)
helm:
  takeOwnership: true
=== 15-cert-manager/fleet.yaml ===
# Fleet bundle — cert-manager (Helm).
#
# Pinned to v1.20.2, matching the running release, so Fleet adopts rather than
# upgrades.
#
# THIS IS THE MOST LOAD-BEARING BUNDLE IN THE REPO AFTER LONGHORN. It issues
# every TLS certificate in the cluster — 8 Certificates across ai, hermes,
# lab-memory, ollama-code and registry, all through the single cluster-scoped
# letsencrypt-dns ClusterIssuer in ./issuer. Break it and TLS fails everywhere,
# though not immediately: existing certs keep serving until renewal.
#
# BEFORE ADOPTING, read values.yaml. It carries two extraArgs that exist only
# on the live Deployment and NOT in the recorded release. Omitting them is a
# delayed, cluster-wide certificate outage rather than an immediate one.
#
# Adoption restarts the cert-manager controller pod exactly once. The rendered
# arg SET is identical to live, but the chart emits extraArgs before
# --max-concurrent-challenges while live has them after it. Order is still part
# of the pod template, so the Deployment rolls. Nothing is reconfigured.
# cert-manager is stateless and re-reconciles on start; in-flight Challenges
# are retried.
#
# CRDs are chart-managed (crds.enabled: true), so this bundle owns 6
# CustomResourceDefinitions. That is why it is adopted LAST despite platform
# components normally coming first: if Fleet ever prunes this bundle it takes
# the CRDs with it, and every Certificate, Issuer and Order object in the
# cluster goes too. Do not delete this GitRepo to "roll back" — remove the path
# instead, and never enable correctDrift here until everything else is stable.
#
# Numbered 15 rather than inserted before 01 because renumbering the existing
# 00-14 tree would invalidate every GitRepo path and doc reference in the repo.
# Install order and directory order diverge here; see README.md.
defaultNamespace: cert-manager
helm:
  releaseName: cert-manager
  repo: https://charts.jetstack.io
  chart: cert-manager
  version: "v1.20.2"
  valuesFiles:
    - values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true
=== 15-cert-manager/issuer/fleet.yaml ===
# Fleet bundle — letsencrypt-dns ClusterIssuer (raw manifest).
#
# Separate path from ../ because 15-cert-manager is a Helm bundle and Fleet
# allows one chart per path.
#
# ORDERING: the ClusterIssuer is a cert-manager CRD instance, so the CRDs must
# exist before this applies. In practice they already do (the cluster has been
# issuing certs since June), but on a rebuild adopt ../ first.
#
# PREREQUISITE SECRET: cloudflare-api-token (key: api-token) in the
# cert-manager namespace — the Cloudflare API token for the DNS-01 solver. Not
# in this repo. Verified present 2026-07-30.
#
# Verified `kubectl diff`-clean against live before adoption.
defaultNamespace: cert-manager

# Raw-manifest bundle, but Fleet still deploys it via Helm internally — so
# adopting the objects that are already on the cluster needs takeOwnership.
# Without it the first sync fails: the live objects carry no
# meta.helm.sh/release-name annotation, and Helm refuses to touch resources it
# does not believe it owns. With it, adoption is metadata-only (Helm labels on
# the top-level objects), so no pod template changes and no restarts.
helm:
  takeOwnership: true
=== 05-open-webui/fleet.yaml ===
# Fleet bundle — Open WebUI (Helm). See fleet-wiring-plan Phase 1.
# StatefulSet-backed chat UI. No Secret prerequisite — the earlier note here
# claimed WEBUI_SECRET_KEY was required, but the live StatefulSet references no
# Secret at all and none exists in the ai namespace.
#
# values.yaml points both Ollama URLs at ollama-exporter:9401 (the pass-through
# proxy), matching the live object. The release itself still declared
# ollama:11434 — drift that `helm get values` could not show. Diff
# `helm get manifest` against the cluster before adopting.
defaultNamespace: ai
helm:
  releaseName: open-webui
  repo: https://helm.openwebui.com/
  chart: open-webui
  version: "14.8.0"
  valuesFiles:
    - values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true
=== 17-buzz/fleet.yaml ===
# Fleet bundle — Buzz relay (Helm).
#
# Nostr-based messaging relay at buzz.ash4d.com: one relay binary serving
# WebSocket + REST + web UI, backed by bundled PostgreSQL and Redis subcharts.
#
# Chart pinned to 0.1.6, matching the running release, so Fleet adopts rather
# than upgrades. Verified: renders byte-identical to live.
#
# The chart lives at oci://ghcr.io/block/buzz/charts/buzz — note the `/charts/`
# path segment. This bundle briefly vendored a copy of the chart recovered from
# the live Helm release secret, on the mistaken conclusion that 0.1.6 was
# unpublished. It is published; the earlier check probed
# oci://ghcr.io/block/buzz (no `/charts/`) and got a 404. The correct ref was
# recorded all along in this directory's values.yaml header and in shell history.
# The recovered copy rendered identically to what upstream serves, so nothing was
# wrong with the output — only with vendoring ~36 files that did not need to be
# in this repo. Lesson recorded in FLEET-WIRING.md: before concluding a chart is
# lost, pull the exact ref from the install command, not a guessed one.
#
# `github.com/block/buzz` is an unrelated audio-transcription desktop app, which
# is a red herring — the chart's own `home:`/`sources:` URLs point at it.
#
# Subcharts (postgres, redis from oci://registry-1.docker.io/cloudpirates) come
# from the published chart's own Chart.lock, so there is nothing to vendor and no
# `helm dependency build` for Fleet to run.
#
# PREREQUISITE SECRET: `buzz-relay` must exist in the namespace before this
# path is enabled. values.yaml sets secrets.existingSecret, which suppresses
# the chart's own Secret; the Postgres and Redis subcharts still read
# postgres-password / redis-password from that same name. See the buzz-relay
# repo's secret.md for the full required key list.
#
# TLS: there is deliberately NO tls block and NO cert-manager Certificate for
# buzz.ash4d.com on this cluster. TLS terminates at a GCP edge proxy, and both
# clusters run a Cloudflare DNS-01 solver against the same zone — if both
# issued for this host they would race on the same _acme-challenge TXT record
# at renewal time, unattended. Exactly one cluster owns that cert and it is
# GCP. This is why buzz-ext-ash4d-tls is a hand-made Secret here rather than a
# cert-manager Certificate. Do not "fix" this by adding an issuer annotation.
#
# The image is pinned by digest, split across image.repository and image.tag
# because the chart's helper does printf "%s:%s". The current pin is a
# SECURITY floor, not just a version choice: it is the first build containing
# the nostr 0.44.6 bump for RUSTSEC-2026-0216 (NIP-44 remote DoS). Do not roll
# back below it — see the comments in values.yaml.
#
# NOT vendored from the buzz-relay repo: gcp-proxy.yaml and gcp-ollama.yaml.
# Those are applied to a DIFFERENT cluster (the GCP k3s instance), not this
# one, so they are not lab-fleet's cluster state.
defaultNamespace: buzz
helm:
  releaseName: buzz
  chart: oci://ghcr.io/block/buzz/charts/buzz
  version: "0.1.6"
  valuesFiles:
    - values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true
=== 20-openshell/fleet.yaml ===
# Fleet bundle — OpenShell agent gateway (Helm, VENDORED chart).
#
# The chart is vendored under ./chart instead of being pulled from
# oci://ghcr.io/nvidia/openshell/helm-chart, and that is deliberate.
#
# Upstream publishes this chart only as version `0.0.0-dev` — a mutable tag.
# It has ALREADY drifted from the bits that produced the live release: pulling
# 0.0.0-dev on 2026-07-30 yields a chart with an added
# `server.workspaceStorageClass` value, added supervisor sidecar-topology
# options, and a rewritten _helpers.tpl. Pinning `version: 0.0.0-dev` the way
# 04-ollama pins 1.67.0 would therefore NOT adopt the release — it would
# silently upgrade it. There is no immutable version to pin, so the chart that
# is actually running is committed here instead.
#
# ./chart was recovered from the live Helm release secret
# (openshell/sh.helm.release.v1.openshell.v3) — the release stores the chart
# verbatim, so it is exact. Verified: `helm template` against ./chart with
# values.yaml renders byte-identical to live across all three groups it
# touches (openshell, nemoclaw-sandboxes, and the cluster-scoped pair).
#
# Re-check against upstream before any deliberate upgrade; do not assume
# 0.0.0-dev is a safe target.
#
# ORDERING CONSTRAINT: this chart renders a ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding
# and NetworkPolicy into the `nemoclaw-sandboxes` namespace, which is created
# by 19-nemoclaw. Adopt 19-nemoclaw FIRST. It also creates a cluster-scoped
# ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding pair (openshell-node-reader).
#
# values.yaml was recovered from the live release, NOT copied from the
# nemoclaw-ops-agent repo's deploy/openshell/values.yaml. Those disagree, and
# the repo's copy is stale:
#   - repo says `sandboxNamespace: nemoclaw`, live says `nemoclaw-sandboxes`
#   - live also sets `server.auth.allowUnauthenticatedUsers: true`, which the
#     repo copy does not mention at all
# Applying the repo's copy would move the sandbox namespace out from under the

#
# Chart pinned to 0.32.0, matching the running release, so Fleet adopts rather
# than upgrades. All the interesting decisions are in values.yaml — read its
# header before touching anything, especially the two Secret notes.
#
# THIS IS THE ONE ADOPTION IN THIS BATCH THAT RESTARTS A POD. The live
# StatefulSet carries OCR_USE_LLM as its FIRST env entry; the chart emits env
# alphabetically, so OCR_USE_LLM renders between NEXTAUTH_URL and
# OLLAMA_BASE_URL. Same variable, same value, different position — which is
# still a pod-template change, so the karakeep StatefulSet rolls once on
# adoption. Nothing is being reconfigured; the live object had simply been
# hand-edited outside Helm. Expect exactly one karakeep pod replacement and no
# change to karakeep-chrome or karakeep-meilesearch.
#
# PREREQUISITE SECRETS (both already exist; this bundle does NOT manage them,
# see values.yaml note 1):
#   karakeep              — NEXTAUTH_SECRET
#   karakeep-meilesearch  — MEILI_MASTER_KEY   (note the chart's spelling)
# If either is missing when this path is enabled, karakeep comes up without a
# session secret and Meilisearch rejects every query.
#
# The MCP servers, the ingest CronJob and the karakeep Certificate are raw
# manifests and live in ./raw — separate path, because Fleet allows one chart
# per path.

helm:

  chart: karakeep
  version: "0.32.0"
  valuesFiles:

1	# 21 — Unsloth Studio
2	
3	Web GUI for LLM fine-tuning (LoRA/QLoRA and full fine-tuning) on the V100,
4	from the official `unsloth/unsloth` image — Studio UI on 8000 at
5	[unsloth.ash4d.com](https://unsloth.ash4d.com), Jupyter Lab on 8888 at
6	[jupyter.ash4d.com](https://jupyter.ash4d.com). SSH (port 22 in the image) is
7	deliberately not exposed.
8	
9	## Install
10	
11	The Secret must exist **before** the Fleet path is enabled or the pod sticks
12	in `CreateContainerConfigError`:
13	
14	```bash
15	kubectl -n ai create secret generic unsloth-jupyter \
16	  --from-literal=JUPYTER_PASSWORD="$(openssl rand -base64 24)"
17	```
18	
19	Hand-test without Fleet (optional):
20	
21	```bash
22	kubectl apply -f unsloth-studio.yaml
23	```
24	
25	Enable via Fleet by appending this path to the live `lab-ai` GitRepo — read the
26	current list first and append exactly one entry (see
27	`14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/README.md`):
28	
29	```bash
30	kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default get gitrepo lab-ai -o jsonpath='{.spec.paths}'
31	kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default patch gitrepo lab-ai --type=merge \
32	  -p '{"spec":{"paths":[ <current live list...>, "21-unsloth-studio" ]}}'
33	```
34	
35	Unlike the other `lab-ai` paths this is a **fresh install, not an adoption** —
36	Fleet deploys it as soon as the path lands, so the Secret and DNS
37	(`unsloth.ash4d.com`, `jupyter.ash4d.com` → Traefik) must already be in place.
38	
39	## Image / version pinning
40	
41	`unsloth/unsloth` publishes versioned tags; the pinned
42	`2026.5.9-pt2.10.0-vllm-0.16.0-cu12.8-studio-release-v0.1.43-beta-2026-MAY-31`
43	equals the `latest` digest verified 2026-07-30 (`sha256:f21629b9ae4e…`). Bump
44	the tag deliberately — it is a ~13 GB pull, so the first pod start on a new tag
45	is slow. Building a custom image (e.g. on SUSE BCI) was considered and
46	rejected: it would mean recreating the CUDA 12.8 / PyTorch 2.10 / Triton /
47	vLLM stack by hand for zero benefit.
48	
49	The image is CUDA 12.8 — the host driver must satisfy CUDA 12.x compat
50	(`nvidia-smi` on sdf1 shows the driver's max supported CUDA version).
51	
52	## GPU: replicas 0, V100 by UUID
53	
54	Same pattern and same reason as ComfyUI (`07-comfyui/`): GPU access is
55	`runtimeClassName: nvidia` plus an explicit `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` UUID —
56	**not** a device-plugin `nvidia.com/gpu` request, which would let the plugin
57	override the pin and possibly hand out the 8 GB GTX 1070. The pinned UUID is
58	the Tesla V100 that Ollama holds with `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1`, so this
59	Deployment is **declared at `replicas: 0`**.
60	
61	### Starting a fine-tuning session
62	
63	1. Free the V100. Prefer the API unload over scaling ollama (Fleet will fight
64	   `kubectl scale` once `04-ollama` is Fleet-owned):
65	
66	   ```bash
67	   curl http://192.168.7.153/api/generate -d '{"model":"<loaded-model>","keep_alive":0}'
68	   ```
69	
70	   Confirm on the host that the V100 shows ~0 MiB used: `nvidia-smi`.
71	2. Edit `replicas: 1` in `unsloth-studio.yaml`, commit, push; Fleet's 60s poll
72	   picks it up. (Before Fleet owns this path, `kubectl -n ai scale deploy
73	   unsloth-studio --replicas=1` works too.)
74	3. When done, reverse: set `replicas: 0`, then load the ollama model again
75	   (any request to ollama reloads it).
76	
77	### V100 constraints
78	
79	SM 7.0 (Volta): **fp16 only — no bf16, no flash-attention-2.** Pick fp16 in
80	Studio's training options; bf16 runs will fail or silently fall back. 4-bit
81	QLoRA and fp16 LoRA both work; FP8 does not.
82	
83	## Storage
84	
85	One 100Gi Longhorn PVC (`unsloth-data`), single mount at `/workspace/work`
86	(the image's working-directory convention). `HF_HOME` is redirected to
87	`/workspace/work/.hf-home` so the base-model cache, datasets, and checkpoints
88	all live on the one PVC and survive pod restarts — the ComfyUI lesson ("both
89	mounts must be PVC-backed or installs die with the pod") solved with a single
90	mount.
91	
92	100Gi fits a couple of 13B-class fp16 base models plus datasets and LoRA
93	checkpoints. The Longhorn pool was at ~412Gi of ~500Gi allocated before this
94	claim; expand online (Longhorn supports it) rather than over-claiming. Do not
95	run full-model checkpoint-heavy fine-tunes against this pool.
96	
97	## Resources
98	
99	Requests `2 CPU / 8Gi`, limits `6 CPU / 28Gi`. The node is a single 16-thread
100	3700X with 64 GB running everything including the k3s control plane: the low
101	request keeps a `replicas: 0→1` flip schedulable with ollama, milvus, emby et
102	al. resident; the limits cap a runaway tokenization/dataset-prep burst before
103	it starves the node. No GPU resource entries (see above).
104	
105	## Security
106	
107	Jupyter is arbitrary code execution in a GPU pod behind a single password —
108	the `unsloth-jupyter` Secret. Never leave the image default (`unsloth`); the
109	create command above generates a random one. Retrieve it with:
110	
111	```bash
112	kubectl -n ai get secret unsloth-jupyter -o jsonpath='{.data.JUPYTER_PASSWORD}' | base64 -d
113	```
114	
115	TLS on both hosts via cert-manager (`letsencrypt-dns` DNS-01), certs issue
116	even while the Deployment sits at 0 (Traefik 502s until scale-up — expected).

README.md
# Fleet GitRepos — one per namespace

These are Fleet **`GitRepo` custom resources** (`gitrepos.fleet.cattle.io`), not
git repositories. Each one points Fleet at the existing `lab-fleet` repo and
lists which paths to render. They live on the **Rancher controller**
(192.168.7.148, kubectl context `rancher`) — not on sdf1 — so they are not part
of any bundle in this repo. Kept here as the versioned source of record.

    kubectl --context rancher apply -f 14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-node-red.yaml

Applying any file here is a **single** adoption step, and idempotent once adopted —
no file holds more than one unadopted path (see the rule below). The exception is
`lab-ai`, which has **no file at all** and is staged by hand — see below.

> **🔴 Two corrections learned by breaking things on 2026-07-30. Read these
> before adopting anything.**
>
> **1. Removing a path does NOT roll back — it uninstalls.** For a bundle whose
> Helm release Fleet has taken ownership of, deleting the path runs the
> equivalent of `helm uninstall`. This deleted karakeep's StatefulSets,
> Deployment, Service, Ingress and one PVC. Use `spec.paused: true` to stop Fleet
> acting, and fix forward. Only `spec.paths` removal on a bundle that never
> reached ownership is safe.
>
> **2. A nested path is not a staging gate.** Fleet deploys `<path>/<child>` as
> soon as `<path>` is adopted, whether or not the child is in `spec.paths`.
> Gating only works between SIBLING paths (`01-networking` and
> `01-networking/pools`). The "then patch in the second path" note that used to
> appear on `lab-buzz`, `lab-lab-memory` and `lab-cert-manager` was wrong and has
> been corrected.
>
> **3. `kubectl diff` clean does not predict Fleet.** Fleet applies server-side
> and needs field *ownership*. Pre-flight any pre-existing Helm release with
> `kubectl apply --server-side --dry-run=server`, which surfaces the
> field-manager conflicts `kubectl diff` normalises away.
>
> Details and evidence for all three are in `FLEET-WIRING.md`.

## Convention: `lab-<namespace>`

One GitRepo per Kubernetes namespace, so each namespace's workloads can be
adopted, rolled back, or paused independently of every other.

| GitRepo | Namespace | Paths | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lab-nemoclaw` | `nemoclaw` + `nemoclaw-sandboxes` | `19-nemoclaw` | **lowest — start here.** No pod templates at all |
| `lab-node-red` | `node-red` | `12-node-red` | low |
| `lab-emby` | `emby` | `11-emby` | low |
| `lab-resilio` | `resilio` | `13-resilio` | low |
| `lab-ash4d-origin` | `ash4d-origin` | `16-ash4d-origin` | low |
| `lab-hermes` | `hermes` | `10-hermes` | low–med — needs `hermes-webui` Secret |
| `lab-ai` | `ai` | 10 paths (04→09, 21) | med — **no `.yaml` file, staged by hand — see below** |
| `lab-openshell` | `openshell` | `20-openshell` | med — **after `lab-nemoclaw`**; vendored chart |
| `lab-buzz` | `buzz` | `17-buzz` (+ nested `17-buzz/minio`, comes automatically) | med — stateful; needs `buzz-relay` Secret |
| `lab-lab-memory` | `lab-memory` | `18-lab-memory` (+ nested `/raw`) | **ADOPTED** 2026-07-30 after an SSA ownership handoff — zero pod restarts |
| `lab-metallb-system` | `metallb-system` | `01-networking` — then patch in `01-networking/pools` | med–high |
| `lab-nvidia-device-plugin` | `nvidia-device-plugin` | `03-gpu` — `03-gpu/runtimeclass` is **on hold, k3s owns it** | med–high |
| `lab-cattle-monitoring-system` | `cattle-monitoring-system` | `03-gpu/dcgm-exporter` | med |
| `lab-cert-manager` | `cert-manager` | `15-cert-manager` (+ nested `/issuer`) | **ADOPTED** 2026-07-30 after an SSA ownership handoff — owns the 6 CRDs, never delete |
| `lab-longhorn-system` | `longhorn-system` | `02-longhorn` | **highest — adopt last** |

Adopt in that order. Within `lab-ai`, add paths one at a time — raw manifests
(`08-indexer`, `09-mcp`, `07-comfyui`, `06-milvus/attu`,
`04-ollama/ollama-exporter`, `09-mcp/ollama-code`) before the Helm charts
(`04-ollama`, `05-open-webui`, `06-milvus`). `21-unsloth-studio` goes last —
it is a **fresh install, not an adoption**, so Fleet deploys it the moment the
path lands; its `unsloth-jupyter` Secret and DNS must exist first (see
`21-unsloth-studio/README.md`).

Two ordering constraints are hard, not preferences:

- **`lab-nemoclaw` before `lab-openshell`.** The openshell chart renders a
  ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding and NetworkPolicy *into* the
  `nemoclaw-sandboxes` namespace, and `lab-nemoclaw` is what creates that
  namespace. These two are not independently removable.
- **`lab-cert-manager` late, and never deleted.** It owns the six cert-manager
  CRDs, so deleting the GitRepo deletes every `Certificate`, `Issuer` and
  `Order` object in the cluster. Roll back by removing the path.

`lab-ash4d-origin`, `lab-nemoclaw` and `lab-openshell` hold a single path each,
so there is nothing to stage for them.

## `lab-ai` deliberately has no `.yaml` file

**There is no `lab-ai.yaml`, on purpose — do not add one.** It used to exist and
listed all eight paths. That made it a footgun: a single `kubectl apply -f` would
widen the GitRepo by however many paths were still unadopted, in one shot, which
is exactly what the one-at-a-time rule exists to prevent. A file whose whole
convention is "apply me" cannot safely hold a staged rollout, so the staging lives
here as commands instead.

Because it has no file, `lab-ai` also misses anything the files carry — notably
`pollingInterval`. It was set by hand and must be re-set if the GitRepo is ever
recreated:

```bash
kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default patch gitrepo lab-ai --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"pollingInterval":"60s"}}'
```

`spec.paths` is the only field that changes between steps, so widen by patching it
and leave everything else alone:

```bash
# Current live state — the five raw-manifest paths (adopted 2026-07-29).
# Append exactly ONE entry per step, in this order:
#   09-mcp/ollama-code → 04-ollama → 05-open-webui → 06-milvus
#     → 21-unsloth-studio (fresh install, deploys immediately — prereqs in
#       21-unsloth-studio/README.md)
kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default patch gitrepo lab-ai --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"paths":[
  "08-indexer","09-mcp","07-comfyui","06-milvus/attu","04-ollama/ollama-exporter",
  "09-mcp/ollama-code"
]}}'
```

`09-mcp/ollama-code` is first in that order because it is the only entry that is
**not** an adoption — it moves the ollama-code MCP server out of its own
`ollama-code` namespace and into `ai`. Read `09-mcp/ollama-code/fleet.yaml`
before running it: the old Ingress must be deleted *first* so two Ingresses
never both claim `mcp-ollama.ash4d.com`, and cert-manager has to issue a fresh

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: unsloth-studio
  name: unsloth-studio
  namespace: ai
spec:
  # DECLARED AT ZERO on purpose: the GPU pin below is the same V100 that ollama
  # holds with OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1 (see 04-ollama/values.yaml), so the two
  # cannot both be resident. Scale to 1 when you want a fine-tuning session and
  # can afford to evict ollama's model (procedure in README.md).
  # Fleet will hold this at 0 — bump it here, not with `kubectl scale`, or the
  # next reconcile puts it back.
  replicas: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: unsloth-studio
  # Recreate, not RollingUpdate: the data PVC is RWO and the GPU is exclusive,
  # so old and new pods can never overlap.
  strategy:
    type: Recreate
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: unsloth-studio
    spec:
      containers:
      - env:
        # GPU pin: the Tesla V100 32GB, NOT GPU 0 (a GTX 1070, 8GB). Same UUID
        # ollama's chart pins (04-ollama/values.yaml) — that pair is the whole
        # reason this Deployment sits at replicas: 0.
        # V100 is SM 7.0: fp16 only — no bf16, no flash-attention-2. Studio
        # training runs must select fp16.
        - name: NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
          value: GPU-a69c6398-0353-3234-9f35-af0e02865f33
        - name: NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES
          value: compute,utility
        # Jupyter (and the Studio UI's auth) password. Secret is created by
        # hand, never committed — command in README.md. The image default
        # ("unsloth") must never survive: jupyter.ash4d.com is code execution
        # in a GPU pod behind this one credential.
        - name: JUPYTER_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: JUPYTER_PASSWORD
              name: unsloth-jupyter
        # Steer the HF model/tokenizer cache under the single PVC mount so a
        # pod restart never re-downloads base models. Everything that must
        # survive a restart (datasets, checkpoints, adapters, HF cache) lives
        # under /workspace/work.
        - name: HF_HOME
          value: /workspace/work/.hf-home
        # Pinned tag == the `latest` digest verified 2026-07-30
        # (sha256:f21629b9ae4e…). Upstream publishes versioned tags regularly;
        # bump deliberately, never track latest — this is a ~13 GB pull.
        image: unsloth/unsloth:2026.5.9-pt2.10.0-vllm-0.16.0-cu12.8-studio-release-v0.1.43-beta-2026-MAY-31
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent

# Fleet GitRepo — openshell namespace.
#
# This is the Fleet `GitRepo` CUSTOM RESOURCE (gitrepos.fleet.cattle.io), not a
# git repository: it points Fleet at the existing lab-fleet repo and tells it
# which paths to render. It lives on the RANCHER CONTROLLER
# (192.168.7.148, kubectl context `rancher`), so it is not part of any bundle here.
#
#   kubectl --context rancher apply -f 14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-openshell.yaml
#
# One GitRepo per namespace — see gitrepos/README.md.
#
# MED RISK. The chart is VENDORED, and that is not a stylistic choice:
# upstream publishes only the MUTABLE tag `0.0.0-dev`, which has ALREADY
# drifted from the running release. Pinning that tag would silently
# upgrade openshell instead of adopting it. See 20-openshell/fleet.yaml.
# Verified: the vendored chart renders identically to live.
#
# ADOPT AFTER lab-nemoclaw. This chart writes a ServiceAccount, Role,
# RoleBinding and NetworkPolicy into the `nemoclaw-sandboxes` namespace,
# which lab-nemoclaw creates. It also owns a cluster-scoped
# ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding pair (openshell-node-reader).
#
# values.yaml came from the live release, NOT from the nemoclaw-ops-agent
# repo's deploy/openshell/values.yaml — those disagree on
# sandboxNamespace and the repo copy is stale.
#
# Single path — nothing staged.
apiVersion: fleet.cattle.io/v1alpha1
kind: GitRepo
metadata:
  name: lab-openshell
  namespace: fleet-default
spec:
  repo: https://github.com/darthzen/lab-fleet
  branch: main
  # Explicit polling interval. Fleet's default is 15s, but this cluster's
  # gitjob runs with `gitjob.syncPeriod: 2h` (a Rancher fleet-chart value), and
  # on 2026-07-30 four GitRepos went dormant for 28+ minutes after a single
  # transient `context deadline exceeded` against github.com -- they only
  # recovered when an external write forced a reconcile. Stating the interval
  # here bounds how stale a repo can get and makes the intent reviewable in git
  # rather than depending on a controller-wide default. See FLEET-WIRING.md.
  pollingInterval: 60s
  paths:
    - 20-openshell
  # `ash4d-lab` is a bespoke label already on the sdf1 cluster (c-nnzn9). Chosen
  # over management.cattle.io/cluster-name, which Rancher owns and may rewrite.
  # Do NOT reuse site=ash4d — that belongs to the ash4d-site GitRepo and resolves
  # to a different downstream cluster.
  targets:
    - clusterSelector:
        matchLabels:
          ash4d-lab: ""
  # correctDrift OFF until every namespace is adopted and verified. Turning it on
  # makes Fleet revert out-of-band `kubectl edit`s — the eventual goal, but it
  # will fight this cluster's hand-tuning habits (GPU pins, context sizes).
  correctDrift:
    enabled: false

d=json.load(sys.stdin)
tags=d.get("tags",[])
sem=[t for t in tags if re.match(r"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$",t)]

result.output:
# OpenChoreo Installation Prerequisites & Commands

## Prerequisites

**Cluster Requirements:**
- "Kubernetes 1.33+, LoadBalancer support, and a default StorageClass"
- Linux nodes with kernel 6.3+, containerd 2.0+ or CRI-O 1.25+, runc 1.2+ or crun 1.9+
- Tools: kubectl v1.33+, Helm v3.12+

## Prerequisite Components (Install Order)

### 1. Gateway API CRDs
```bash
kubectl apply --server-side \
  -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.5.1/standard-install.yaml
```

### 2. cert-manager
```bash
helm upgrade --install cert-manager oci://quay.io/jetstack/charts/cert-manager \
  --namespace cert-manager \
  --create-namespace \
  --version v1.19.4 \
  --set crds.enabled=true \
  --wait --timeout 180s
```

### 3. External Secrets Operator
```bash
helm upgrade --install external-secrets oci://ghcr.io/external-secrets/charts/external-secrets \
  --namespace external-secrets \
  --create-namespace \
  --version 2.0.1 \
  --set installCRDs=true \
  --wait --timeout 180s
```

### 4. kgateway CRDs
```bash
helm upgrade --install kgateway-crds oci://cr.kgateway.dev/kgateway-dev/charts/kgateway-crds \
  --create-namespace --namespace openchoreo-control-plane \
  --version v2.3.1
```

### 5. kgateway
```bash
helm upgrade --install kgateway oci://cr.kgateway.dev/kgateway-dev/charts/kgateway \
  --namespace openchoreo-control-plane --create-namespace \
  --version v2.3.1
```

### 6. OpenBao (Secret Backend)
```bash
helm upgrade --install openbao oci://ghcr.io/openbao/charts/openbao \
  --namespace openbao \
  --create-namespace \
  --version 0.25.6 \
  --values https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openchoreo/openchoreo/release-v1.2/install/k3d/common/values-openbao.yaml \
  --wait --timeout 300s
```

### 7. ThunderID (Identity Provider)
```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openchoreo/openchoreo/release-v1.2/install/k3d/common/values-thunder.yaml \
| sed "s#http://thunder.openchoreo.localhost:8080#https://thunder.${CP_BASE_DOMAIN}#g" \
| sed "s#http://openchoreo.localhost:8080#https://console.${CP_BASE_DOMAIN}#g" \
| helm upgrade --install thunder oci://ghcr.io/asgardeo/helm-charts/thunder \
  --namespace thunder \
  --create-namespace \
  --version 0.28.0 \
  --values -
```

## Main OpenChoreo Planes

### Control Plane (v1.2.1)
```bash
helm upgrade --install openchoreo-control-plane oci://ghcr.io/openchoreo/helm-charts/openchoreo-control-plane \
  --version 1.2.1 \
  --namespace openchoreo-control-plane \
  --create-namespace \
  --values [config-with-hostnames-and-tls]
```

### Data Plane (v1.2.1)
```bash
helm upgrade --install openchoreo-data-plane oci://ghcr.io/openchoreo/helm-charts/openchoreo-data-plane \
  --version 1.2.1 \
  --namespace openchoreo-data-plane \
  --create-namespace \
  --set gateway.tls.enabled=false
```

### Workflow Plane (v1.2.1, Optional)
```bash
helm upgrade --install openchoreo-workflow-plane oci://ghcr.io/openchoreo/helm-charts/openchoreo-workflow-plane \
  --version 1.2.1 \
  --namespace openchoreo-workflow-plane \
  --create-namespace \
  --set clusterAgent.tls.generateCerts=true
```

### Observability Plane (v1.2.1, Optional)
```bash
helm upgrade --install openchoreo-observability-plane oci://ghcr.io/openchoreo/helm-charts/openchoreo-observability-plane \
  --version 1.2.1 \
  --namespace openchoreo-observability-plane \
  --create-namespace \
  --timeout 25m \
  --values [config-with-observer-settings]
```

## Required Values Patterns

All planes need hostnames, TLS certificate references (from cert-manager), and secret store references. "Self-signed certificates by default; swap in certificates from a real CA later" for production use.

install_control_plane() {

apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: backstage-secrets
  namespace: ${CONTROL_PLANE_NS}
spec:
  refreshInterval: 1h
  secretStoreRef:
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
    name: default
  target:
    name: backstage-secrets
  data:
    - secretKey: backend-secret

    - secretKey: client-secret

        --from-literal=ca.crt="$ca_crt" \
        -n "$CONTROL_PLANE_NS" --dry-run=client -o yaml | $KUBECTL apply -f -
}

install_default_resources() {
    step "Installing default resources"
    $KUBECTL label namespace default openchoreo.dev/control-plane=true --overwrite
    $KUBECTL apply -f "$(asset samples/getting-started/all.yaml)"
}

# copy_gateway_ca <namespace> — give a plane's agent the cluster-gateway CA
copy_gateway_ca() {
    local ns="$1"
    $KUBECTL create namespace "$ns" --dry-run=client -o yaml | $KUBECTL apply -f -
    local ca_crt
    ca_crt=$($KUBECTL get configmap cluster-gateway-ca -n "$CONTROL_PLANE_NS" -o jsonpath='{.data.ca\.crt}')
    $KUBECTL create configmap cluster-gateway-ca \
        --from-literal=ca.crt="$ca_crt" \
        -n "$ns" --dry-run=client -o yaml | $KUBECTL apply -f -
}

# agent_ca <namespace> <certificate> — wait for the agent cert to be issued, then echo its CA.
agent_ca() {
    local ns="$1" cert="$2"
    $KUBECTL wait -n "$ns" --for=condition=Ready "certificate/$cert" --timeout=120s >&2
    $KUBECTL get secret cluster-agent-tls -n "$ns" -o jsonpath='{.data.ca\.crt}' | base64 -d
}

install_data_plane() {
    step "Installing the data plane"
    copy_gateway_ca "$DATA_PLANE_NS"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2046
    $HELM upgrade --install openchoreo-data-plane "$HELM_REPO/openchoreo-data-plane" \
        $(chart_version_args) \
        --namespace "$DATA_PLANE_NS" --create-namespace \
        --values "$(asset install/k3d/single-cluster/values-dp.yaml)"

    step "Registering the data plane"
    local ca; ca=$(agent_ca "$DATA_PLANE_NS" cluster-agent-dataplane-tls)
    $KUBECTL apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: openchoreo.dev/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterDataPlane
metadata:
  name: default
spec:
  planeID: default
  clusterAgent:
    clientCA:
      value: |
$(echo "$ca" | sed 's/^/        /')
  secretStoreRef:
    name: default

    ingress:

install_observability_plane() {
    step "Installing the observability plane"

    step "Creating observability ExternalSecrets"
    $KUBECTL apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: opensearch-admin-credentials
  namespace: ${OBSERVABILITY_NS}
spec:
  refreshInterval: 1h
  secretStoreRef:
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
    name: default
  target:
    name: opensearch-admin-credentials
  data:
    - secretKey: username
      remoteRef: { key: opensearch-username, property: value }
    - secretKey: password
      remoteRef: { key: opensearch-password, property: value }
---
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: observer-secret
  namespace: ${OBSERVABILITY_NS}
spec:
  refreshInterval: 1h
  secretStoreRef:
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
    name: default
  target:
    name: observer-secret
  data:
    - secretKey: UID_RESOLVER_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
      remoteRef: { key: observer-oauth-client-secret, property: value }
EOF

        --for=condition=Ready externalsecret/opensearch-admin-credentials \
        externalsecret/observer-secret --timeout=120s

        "[ -s /etc/machine-id ] || cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid | tr -d '-' > /etc/machine-id"

        $(chart_version_args) \
        --namespace "$OBSERVABILITY_NS" \
        --values "$(asset install/k3d/single-cluster/values-op.yaml)" \
        --timeout 25m

    step "Installing observability modules"

        oci://ghcr.io/openchoreo/helm-charts/observability-logs-opensearch \
        --namespace "$OBSERVABILITY_NS" --version "$LOGS_OPENSEARCH_VERSION" \
        --set openSearchSetup.openSearchSecretName="opensearch-admin-credentials" \
        --set adapter.openSearchSecretName="opensearch-admin-credentials"
    $HELM upgrade --install observability-traces-opensearch \
        oci://ghcr.io/openchoreo/helm-charts/observability-tracing-opensearch \
        --namespace "$OBSERVABILITY_NS" --version "$TRACES_OPENSEARCH_VERSION" \
        --set openSearch.enabled=false \
        --set openSearchSetup.openSearchSecretName="opensearch-admin-credentials"
    $HELM upgrade --install observability-metrics-prometheus \
        oci://ghcr.io/openchoreo/helm-charts/observability-metrics-prometheus \
        --namespace "$OBSERVABILITY_NS" --version "$METRICS_PROMETHEUS_VERSION"
    $HELM upgrade observability-logs-opensearch \
        oci://ghcr.io/openchoreo/helm-charts/observability-logs-opensearch \
        --namespace "$OBSERVABILITY_NS" --version "$LOGS_OPENSEARCH_VERSION" \
        --reuse-values --set fluent-bit.enabled=true

    # Collect Kubernetes events into the k8s-events OpenSearch index.
    $HELM upgrade --install observability-events-otel-collector \
        oci://ghcr.io/openchoreo/helm-charts/observability-events-otel-collector \
        --namespace "$OBSERVABILITY_NS" --version "$EVENTS_OTEL_COLLECTOR_VERSION" \
        -f - <<'EOF'
collector:
  extraEnv:
    - name: OPENSEARCH_USERNAME
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: opensearch-admin-credentials
          key: username
    - name: OPENSEARCH_PASSWORD
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: opensearch-admin-credentials
          key: password
extraExtensions:
  basicauth/opensearch:
    client_auth:
      username: ${env:OPENSEARCH_USERNAME}
      password: ${env:OPENSEARCH_PASSWORD}
exporters:
  opensearch:
    logs_index: "k8s-events"
    logs_index_time_format: "yyyy-MM-dd"

      #!/bin/bash
      set -e

      THUNDER_URL="http://localhost:8090"

      log_info "Checking if default organization unit exists..."
      if ! curl -s --max-time 10 "${THUNDER_URL}/organization-units" | grep -q '"handle" *: *"default"'; then
        log_info "Creating default organization unit..."
        curl --location "${THUNDER_URL}/organization-units" \
          --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
          --header 'Accept: application/json' \
          --data '{
            "name": "Default",
            "handle": "default",

          }' \
          --fail-with-body \
          --max-time 30 \
          --retry 3 \
          --retry-delay 5
        log_info "Default organization unit created successfully"
      else
        log_info "Default organization unit already exists"
      fi

      ORG_UNIT_ID=$(curl -s --max-time 10 "${THUNDER_URL}/organization-units/tree/default" | grep -o '"id":"[^"]*"' | head -1 | cut -d'"' -f4)
      if [ -z "$ORG_UNIT_ID" ]; then
        log_error "Failed to resolve default organization unit ID from ${THUNDER_URL}"
        exit 1
      fi
      log_info "Using organization unit ID: $ORG_UNIT_ID"

      log_info "Checking if user schema 'openchoreo-user' already exists..."
      existing_schemas=$(curl -s --max-time 10 "${THUNDER_URL}/user-schemas")

      if echo "$existing_schemas" | grep -q '"name" *: *"openchoreo-user"'; then
        log_info "User schema 'openchoreo-user' already exists, skipping creation"
      else
        log_info "User schema does not exist, creating user schema..."
        curl --location "${THUNDER_URL}/user-schemas" \
          --header 'accept: application/json' \
          --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
          --data "{
            \"name\": \"openchoreo-user\",
            \"ouId\": \"$ORG_UNIT_ID\",
            \"allowSelfRegistration\": true,
            \"systemAttributes\": {
              \"display\": \"username\"
            },
            \"schema\": {
              \"username\": {
                \"type\": \"string\",
                \"required\": true,
                \"displayName\": \"Username\"
              },
              \"password\": {
                \"type\": \"string\",
                \"required\": true,
                \"credential\": true,
                \"displayName\": \"Password\"
              },
              \"given_name\": {
                \"type\": \"string\",
                \"required\": true,
                \"displayName\": \"First Name\"
              },
              \"family_name\": {
                \"type\": \"string\",
                \"required\": true,
                \"displayName\": \"Last Name\"
              },
              \"email\": {
                \"type\": \"string\",
                \"required\": true,
                \"unique\": true,
                \"displayName\": \"Email\"
              }
            }
          }" \
          --fail-with-body \
          --max-time 30 \
          --retry 3 \
          --retry-delay 5

        log_info "User schema created successfully"
      fi

      # Returns the ID of an existing user by username, or creates and returns it.
      # Usage: ensure_user <username> <password> <given_name> <family_name>
      ensure_user() {
        local username="$1" password="$2" given_name="$3" family_name="$4"
        local existing_users user_id response

        existing_users=$(curl -s --max-time 10 "${THUNDER_URL}/users")
        if echo "$existing_users" | grep -q "\"username\" *: *\"${username}\""; then
          log_info "User '${username}' already exists, getting ID..." >&2
          user_id=$(echo "$existing_users" | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/" *: *"/":"/g' \
            | grep -o "\"username\":\"${username}\"[^}]*\"id\":\"[^\"]*\"\|\"id\":\"[^\"]*\"[^}]*\"username\":\"${username}\"" \
            | grep -o '"id":"[^"]*"' | head -1 | cut -d'"' -f4)
        else
          log_info "Creating user '${username}'..." >&2
          response=$(curl --location "${THUNDER_URL}/users" \
            --header 'accept: application/json' \
            --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
            --data "{
              \"type\": \"openchoreo-user\",
              \"organizationUnit\": \"$ORG_UNIT_ID\",
              \"attributes\": {
                \"username\": \"${username}\",
                \"email\": \"${username}\",
                \"password\": \"${password}\",
                \"given_name\": \"${given_name}\",
                \"family_name\": \"${family_name}\"
              }
            }" \
            --fail-with-body \
            --max-time 30 \
            --retry 3 \
            --retry-delay 5)
          log_info "User '${username}' created successfully" >&2
          user_id=$(echo "$response" | grep -o '"id":"[^"]*"' | head -1 | cut -d'"' -f4)
        fi
        echo "$user_id"
      }

      # Creates a group with a single member if it does not already exist.
      # Usage: ensure_group <group_name> <description> <member_user_id>
      ensure_group() {
        local group_name="$1" description="$2" member_id="$3"
        local existing_groups group_members

        existing_groups=$(curl -s --max-time 10 "${THUNDER_URL}/groups")
        if echo "$existing_groups" | grep -q "\"name\" *: *\"${group_name}\""; then

        if [ -n "$member_id" ]; then
          group_members="{\"type\":\"user\",\"id\":\"${member_id}\"}"
        fi

        log_info "Creating group '${group_name}'..."
        curl --location "${THUNDER_URL}/groups" \
          --header 'accept: application/json' \
          --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
          --data "{
            \"name\": \"${group_name}\",
            \"organizationUnitId\": \"$ORG_UNIT_ID\",
            \"description\": \"${description}\",
            \"members\": [${group_members}]
          }" \
          --fail-with-body \
          --max-time 30 \
          --retry 3 \
          --retry-delay 5
        log_info "Group '${group_name}' created successfully"

#
# ESO is how every OpenChoreo credential reaches a pod: the planes' charts take
# a `secretName`, and the Secret behind it is materialised by an ExternalSecret
# pulling from OpenBao through the `default` ClusterSecretStore
# (../secret-store/). OpenChoreo also exposes this to developers as its own
# Secret-management feature — `features.secretManagement.enabled: true` in
# ../control-plane/values.yaml and `secretStoreRef` on the ClusterDataPlane in
# ../registration/ both resolve through this operator.
#
# Version 2.0.1 is what OpenChoreo v1.2's own installer pins
# (install/k3d/k3d-prerequisites.sh). Not a floating tag.
#
# THIS BUNDLE OWNS CLUSTER-SCOPED CRDs (`installCRDs: true`), so deleting it
# takes every ExternalSecret and ClusterSecretStore object with it — the same
# hazard as 15-cert-manager. Roll back by pausing the GitRepo, never by
# deleting this path. See 14-cluster-mgmt/FLEET-WIRING.md.
#
# Nothing else on this cluster uses ESO today, so there is no adoption
# question: this is a fresh install into a fresh namespace.
defaultNamespace: external-secrets

# on every pod restart and must be manually unsealed before OpenChoreo's
# credentials resolve again". On an unattended single-node lab that is the
# worse failure mode. The cost is that OpenBao holds no state you can add to
# by hand and expect to survive — anything you put in it must be added to the
# postStart script in values.yaml.

# wipes the store and reseeds it from values.yaml. ExternalSecrets re-resolve
# on their next refresh (1h) or immediately if you delete them. Nothing is

# deployment's secret management for anything you cannot recreate.

# OpenBao — the secret backend OpenChoreo reads through External Secrets.
#
# Vendored from the OpenChoreo repo at release-v1.2
# (install/k3d/common/values-openbao.yaml), with the sample-app secrets
# dropped and the k3d-only OpenObserve entries dropped (this lab uses the
# OpenSearch modules, not OpenObserve — see ../observability-logs/).
#
# ─── Why dev mode ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# `server.dev.enabled: true` means in-memory storage, auto-unsealed, with a
# fixed root token. The postStart hook below re-runs on every pod start, so
# the auth backend, the two policies, the two roles and every seeded key are
# rebuilt automatically after any restart.
#
# The alternative was `server.standalone` with file storage on a Longhorn PVC.
# It persists, but a sealed OpenBao is indistinguishable from a broken one to
# everything downstream: after every node reboot, ExternalSecrets would stop
# resolving and Backstage and the observer would come up without credentials,
# until someone typed the unseal keys by hand. There is no auto-unseal without
# a KMS. For a single-node lab that nobody is paged for, "reseeds itself" beats
# "persists but needs a human", so dev mode is the deliberate choice.
#
# The corollary is in fleet.yaml and it is not optional reading: secrets added
# to this store by hand, or through OpenChoreo's own secret-management UI, do
# not survive a restart. Only what is written below does.
#
# The root token is `root`. In dev mode that is OpenBao's well-known constant,
# not a credential — the API is ClusterIP-only and nothing routes to it from
# the gateway. Do not "fix" it by setting a different literal here; if this
# ever needs to be a real vault, the fix is file storage plus a real unseal
# procedure, not a different dev token.
#
# ─── Why the seeded values are in git ────────────────────────────────────────
# 🔴 These are OpenChoreo's UPSTREAM FIXTURE CREDENTIALS, published in
# github.com/openchoreo/openchoreo, and every one of them must byte-match the
# corresponding client_secret in ../thunder/values.yaml or the OIDC handshake
# fails. That coupling is why they are literals here rather than env vars from
# a hand-created Secret: Thunder's matching values live inside a 34 KB
# bootstrap shell script in its own values file, so parameterising one side
# without the other would just move the problem.
#
# Acceptable here because the three OpenChoreo hostnames resolve to
# 192.168.7.150 — a LAN address — so none of this is internet-reachable. If
# that changes, rotate BOTH files together. Full procedure in README.md,
# "Rotating the fixture credentials". This and ../thunder/values.yaml are the
# only two files in this repo that carry credential values on purpose.

injector:
  enabled: false

server:
  dev:
    enabled: true
    devRootToken: root

  # Single-node lab: one pod, modest envelope. The chart's default requests
  # are unset, which on this node would let it schedule anywhere; being
  # explicit keeps it accounted for alongside ollama and milvus.
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 50m
      memory: 128Mi
    limits:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 512Mi

  # Runs on every pod start. Everything here must be idempotent, because in
  # dev mode this IS the restore path — there is no persisted state to fall
  # back on.
  postStart:
    - /bin/sh
    - -c
    - |
      sleep 5
      export BAO_ADDR=http://127.0.0.1:8200
      export BAO_TOKEN=root

      bao auth enable kubernetes 2>/dev/null || true
      bao write auth/kubernetes/config \
        kubernetes_host="https://$KUBERNETES_PORT_443_TCP_ADDR:443"

      bao policy write openchoreo-secret-reader-policy - <<POLICY
      path "secret/data/*" { capabilities = ["read"] }
      path "secret/metadata/*" { capabilities = ["list", "read"] }
      POLICY

      bao policy write openchoreo-secret-writer-policy - <<POLICY
      path "secret/data/*" { capabilities = ["create", "read", "update", "delete"] }
      path "secret/metadata/*" { capabilities = ["create", "read", "update", "delete", "list"] }
      POLICY

      # Reader: the `dp*` namespace glob is how OpenChoreo names the
      # namespaces it creates for deployed components, so this is the role a
      # developer's workload authenticates with.
      bao write auth/kubernetes/role/openchoreo-secret-reader-role \
        bound_service_account_names=default \
        bound_service_account_namespaces="dp*" \
        policies=openchoreo-secret-reader-policy ttl=20m

      # Writer: ESO authenticates as the external-secrets-openbao SA in this
      # namespace (see ../secret-store/), and the workflow plane writes build
      # credentials.
      bao write auth/kubernetes/role/openchoreo-secret-writer-role \
        bound_service_account_names="*" \
        bound_service_account_namespaces="openbao,openchoreo-workflow-plane" \
        policies=openchoreo-secret-writer-policy ttl=20m

      # Backstage (the developer portal). backend-secret signs its own
      # sessions; client-secret is its OIDC confidential-client secret and
      # MUST equal the openchoreo-backstage-client secret in
      # ../thunder/values.yaml. The jenkins/github entries are placeholders —
      # ../control-plane/values.yaml leaves both external-CI integrations
      # disabled — but the ExternalSecret in ../control-plane-extras/ lists
      # all five keys, so all five must exist or it never goes Ready.
      bao kv put secret/backstage-backend-secret value="local-dev-backend-secret"
      bao kv put secret/backstage-client-secret value="backstage-portal-secret"
      bao kv put secret/backstage-jenkins-api-key value="placeholder-not-in-use"
      bao kv put secret/backstage-github-actions-token value="placeholder-not-in-use"
      bao kv put secret/backstage-github-oauth-client-secret value="placeholder-not-in-use"

      # Observer (the observability plane's query API). Must equal the
      # openchoreo-observer-resource-reader-client secret in
      # ../thunder/values.yaml.
      bao kv put secret/observer-oauth-client-secret value="openchoreo-observer-resource-reader-client-secret"

      # OpenSearch admin credentials. Must equal
      # openSearch.extraEnvs OPENSEARCH_INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD in
      # ../observability-logs/values.yaml — that env var seeds the OpenSearch
      # security index on FIRST START ONLY, so changing one side later needs
      # an OpenSearch-side password reset, not just a redeploy.
      bao kv put secret/opensearch-username value="admin"
      bao kv put secret/opensearch-password value="ThisIsTheOpenSearchPassword1"

      # RCA and FinOps agents are disabled in
      # ../observability-plane/values.yaml (both want an LLM endpoint and both
      # cost ~1 GiB). Seeded anyway so enabling them is a values change with
      # no OpenBao work — and so these stay next to the Thunder clients they
      # must match.
      bao kv put secret/rca-oauth-client-secret value="openchoreo-rca-agent-secret"
      bao kv put secret/finops-agent-oauth-client-secret value="openchoreo-finops-agent-secret"

# Fleet bundle — kgateway CRDs (Helm). OpenChoreo prerequisite 3 of 4.
#
# Seven cluster-scoped CRDs in the gateway.kgateway.dev group
# (GatewayParameters, TrafficPolicy, HTTPListenerPolicy, Backend, ...). Split
# from ../kgateway/ because upstream ships them as a separate chart and
# because CRDs must exist before anything references them — ../kgateway-params/
# creates a GatewayParameters, and the OpenChoreo control-plane chart renders
# an HTTPListenerPolicy.
#
# 🔴 THIS IS NOT THE GATEWAY API CRDs, AND THIS BUNDLE MUST NEVER SHIP THEM.
# The upstream OpenChoreo installer's first step is
#
#     kubectl apply --server-side -f .../gateway-api/v1.5.1/standard-install.yaml
#
# SKIP IT. gateway.networking.k8s.io v1.5.1 (standard channel) is ALREADY on
# this cluster and is owned by the k3s-bundled `traefik-crd` Helm release in
# kube-system, carrying `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep`. The version is an
# exact match for what OpenChoreo v1.2 wants, so there is nothing to install —
# and installing it anyway would aim Fleet and k3s's addon controller at the
# same cluster-scoped objects. That is the `03-gpu/runtimeclass` failure mode,
# except the blast radius is Traefik's own CRDs and therefore every Ingress in
# the cluster. Leave them to k3s.
#
# If a future OpenChoreo needs a newer Gateway API than k3s ships, that is a
# k3s/Traefik upgrade decision, not something to resolve inside this bundle.
#
# Version v2.3.1 matches OpenChoreo v1.2's installer pin.
#
# DELETING THIS PATH TAKES THE CRDs AND EVERY OBJECT OF THOSE KINDS WITH IT,
# including the GatewayParameters that keeps all three OpenChoreo Gateways off
# the MetalLB pool. Pause the GitRepo instead. See FLEET-WIRING.md.
#
# Namespaced into openchoreo-control-plane only because upstream installs it
# there; the objects it creates are cluster-scoped and the namespace is
# incidental.
defaultNamespace: openchoreo-control-plane
helm:
  releaseName: kgateway-crds
  chart: oci://cr.kgateway.dev/kgateway-dev/charts/kgateway-crds
  version: "v2.3.1"
  takeOwnership: true

# Fleet bundle — shared GatewayParameters for the kgateway GatewayClass
# (raw manifest). OpenChoreo prerequisite 3.5 of 4.
#
# THIS BUNDLE EXISTS FOR ONE REASON: to stop the three OpenChoreo Gateways
# from consuming three MetalLB IPs.
#
# kgateway provisions a Deployment and a Service for every Gateway object, and
# that Service defaults to type LoadBalancer. OpenChoreo creates one Gateway
# per plane — control (../control-plane/), data (../data-plane/) and
# observability (../observability-plane/) — so the default behaviour would
# claim three addresses out of the `lan-pool` 192.168.7.150-169, which had
# exactly five free when this bundle was written. It would also be pointless:
# DNS for openchoreo.ash4d.com, api.openchoreo.ash4d.com and thunder.ash4d.com
# already points at 192.168.7.150, the Traefik LoadBalancer, so traffic
# arrives through Traefik and reaches these Gateways over ClusterIP. See
# ../control-plane-extras/ingress.yaml for the other half of that path.
#
# The object below is referenced class-wide, not per-Gateway:
# ../kgateway/values.yaml sets `gatewayClassParametersRefs.kgateway` to point
# the `kgateway` GatewayClass at it, so all three Gateways inherit ClusterIP
# without any of the three OpenChoreo charts needing a `gateway.infrastructure`
# override. One object, one place to change it.
#
# ORDERING: needs the GatewayParameters CRD from ../kgateway-crds/, and must
# exist before ../kgateway/ reconciles the GatewayClass. Enable in that order.
# A missing referent does not wedge anything permanently — kgateway retries —
# but the Gateways come up as LoadBalancer in the meantime and take the IPs
# this bundle exists to protect.
defaultNamespace: openchoreo-control-plane

# Raw-manifest bundle, but Fleet still deploys it via Helm internally — so
# adopting objects that are already on the cluster needs takeOwnership.
# Without it the first sync fails: live objects carry no
# meta.helm.sh/release-name annotation and Helm refuses to touch resources it
# does not believe it owns. Nothing pre-exists here, so this is a no-op on
# first sync — kept for convention and to protect a future re-adopt after a
# manual `kubectl apply`.
helm:
  takeOwnership: true

# Class-wide defaults for every Gateway of GatewayClass `kgateway`.
#
# Wired in by ../kgateway/values.yaml:
#   gatewayClassParametersRefs:
#     kgateway:
#       name: openchoreo-shared-gwp
#       namespace: openchoreo-control-plane
#
# so it applies to all three OpenChoreo Gateways (control, data and
# observability planes) without any of them declaring
# spec.infrastructure.parametersRef.
apiVersion: gateway.kgateway.dev/v1alpha1
kind: GatewayParameters
metadata:
  name: openchoreo-shared-gwp
  namespace: openchoreo-control-plane
spec:
  kube:
    service:
      # THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS FILE. kgateway's default is LoadBalancer,
      # which would take three addresses from MetalLB's lan-pool
      # (192.168.7.150-169, five free). Traefik at 192.168.7.150 is where the
      # ash4d.com DNS records point, and it reaches these Gateways over
      # ClusterIP — so no OpenChoreo Gateway needs an address of its own.
      # Reverting this to LoadBalancer will silently consume the remaining
      # pool and change nothing about how traffic actually arrives.
      type: ClusterIP

    # Envoy proxy pods, one per Gateway (three of them). The chart ships no
    # resource block at all, which on this node means they schedule
    # unaccounted-for next to ollama, milvus and emby. These are proxies
    # fronting a lab-scale portal, not a production edge.
    envoyContainer:
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu: 50m
          memory: 64Mi
        limits:
          cpu: 500m
          memory: 256Mi

# unimplemented.

  chart: oci://cr.kgateway.dev/kgateway-dev/charts/kgateway
  version: "v2.3.1"
  valuesFiles:

  takeOwnership: true

# kgateway controller — the Gateway API implementation OpenChoreo routes
# through. Upstream's installer passes no values at all; everything here is a
# deliberate adaptation to this cluster.

# THE LOAD-BEARING SETTING. Points the `kgateway` GatewayClass at the shared
# GatewayParameters in ../kgateway-params/, which sets every provisioned
# Gateway Service to ClusterIP instead of the LoadBalancer default. Without
# this, the control, data and observability plane Gateways each claim a
# MetalLB address from lan-pool (192.168.7.150-169, five free) for no benefit —
# DNS points at Traefik on .150 and reaches them over ClusterIP anyway.
#
# The referenced object must exist, so ../kgateway-params/ is enabled first.
# Both name and namespace are required by the chart.
gatewayClassParametersRefs:
  kgateway:
    name: openchoreo-shared-gwp
    namespace: openchoreo-control-plane

controller:
  # Single-node cluster; a second controller replica only waits for a leader
  # lease. Chart default is already 1, stated here so it is a decision rather
  # than an inherited default.
  replicaCount: 1

  # The chart ships no resources block. Being explicit keeps the controller
  # accounted for on a node already at ~50% CPU requests.
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 50m
      memory: 128Mi
    limits:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 512Mi

  # Rancher's kube-prometheus-stack is in cattle-monitoring-system and its
  # operator watches all namespaces (no --namespaces arg, verified
  # 2026-07-30), so a ServiceMonitor here WOULD be picked up. Left off because
  # nothing consumes kgateway control-plane metrics yet; turning it on is a
  # one-line change with no other prerequisite.
  serviceMonitor:
    enabled: false

# Fleet bundle — the `default` ClusterSecretStore (raw manifests).
#
# The join between External Secrets (../external-secrets/) and OpenBao
# (../openbao/): a cluster-scoped store named `default` that authenticates to
# OpenBao with a Kubernetes ServiceAccount token and reads the KV v2 mount at
# `secret/`.
#
# The name `default` is not cosmetic. It is what every consumer references by
# string: the ExternalSecrets in ../control-plane-extras/ and
# ../observability-extras/, and `secretStoreRef.name` on the ClusterDataPlane
# and ClusterWorkflowPlane in ../registration/. Renaming it means editing all
# four.
#
# Separate path from ../openbao/ because Fleet allows one chart per path and
# ../openbao/ is a Helm bundle — the same reason 15-cert-manager/issuer is
# split from 15-cert-manager.
#
# ORDERING: needs the ClusterSecretStore CRD from ../external-secrets/ and a
# reachable OpenBao with the `openchoreo-secret-writer-role` its postStart
# creates. Enable after both. If OpenBao is not up yet the store reports
# NotReady and every ExternalSecret waits — that resolves on its own once
# OpenBao is running; it does not need a redeploy.
#
# Cluster-scoped object: deleting this path breaks every ExternalSecret in the
# OpenChoreo namespaces at once.
defaultNamespace: openbao

# Raw-manifest bundle, but Fleet still deploys it via Helm internally — so
# adopting objects that are already on the cluster needs takeOwnership. Here
# it is a no-op on first sync (nothing pre-exists); kept for convention and to
# protect a future re-adopt after a manual `kubectl apply`.
helm:
  takeOwnership: true

input.content:
# The ServiceAccount External Secrets presents to OpenBao. It needs no RBAC of
# its own — OpenBao's Kubernetes auth backend validates the token and maps it
# to a policy. The binding is on OpenBao's side, in the postStart script of
# ../openbao/values.yaml:
#
#   bao write auth/kubernetes/role/openchoreo-secret-writer-role \
#     bound_service_account_names="*" \
#     bound_service_account_namespaces="openbao,openchoreo-workflow-plane"
#
# — which is why this SA must live in the `openbao` namespace specifically.
# Moving it anywhere else silently fails authentication.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: external-secrets-openbao
  namespace: openbao
---
# Cluster-scoped, and named `default` because four other files reference that
# string (see fleet.yaml).
#
# `provider.vault` is correct despite the backend being OpenBao: OpenBao is a
# Vault fork and speaks the same API, and External Secrets has no separate
# provider for it.
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: ClusterSecretStore
metadata:
  name: default
spec:
  provider:
    vault:
      # In-cluster address. OpenBao is deliberately not routable from the
      # gateway — nothing in ../control-plane-extras/ingress.yaml exposes it.
      server: "http://openbao.openbao.svc:8200"
      path: "secret"
      version: "v2"
      auth:
        kubernetes:
          mountPath: "kubernetes"
          role: "openchoreo-secret-writer-role"
          serviceAccountRef:
            name: "external-secrets-openbao"
            namespace: "openbao"

# the Ingress in ../control-plane-extras/, which forwards to the control

# must byte-match the seeds in ../openbao/values.yaml. Read that file's header
# before touching either. Rotation procedure in README.md.

# pod, and this bundle gives it no PVC — matching upstream's k3d values, where
# the bootstrap Job recreates everything on every start. That is fine for the
# fixture users and clients, and NOT fine for any user you add by hand: those
# do not survive a pod restart. See README.md, "What does not survive a
# restart".

  releaseName: thunder
  chart: oci://ghcr.io/asgardeo/helm-charts/thunder
  version: "0.28.0"
  valuesFiles:

  takeOwnership: true

# Fleet bundle — OpenChoreo control plane (Helm). The core of the platform.
#
# Five workloads: the controller-manager (reconciles the 36 OpenChoreo CRDs),
# the OpenChoreo API server, the Backstage developer portal, the
# cluster-gateway (the mTLS endpoint every other plane's agent dials home to),
# and the event-forwarder.
#
# Chart 1.2.1 == appVersion v1.2.1, the release published 2026-07-30. Pinned,
# not floating: ghcr.io/openchoreo/helm-charts also publishes mutable
# `0.0.0-latest-dev` and ~1000 content-addressed `0.0.0-<sha>` tags, and the
# 20-openshell lesson in FLEET-WIRING.md is that a mutable tag is not a pin.
#
# 🔴 THIS BUNDLE OWNS 36 CLUSTER-SCOPED CRDs (chart `crds/` directory). Same
# hazard class as 15-cert-manager: deleting this path uninstalls the release,
# which takes the CRDs and therefore every Project, Component, Workload and
# plane-registration object in the cluster. Pause the GitRepo to stop Fleet
# acting; never remove the path to "roll back". See FLEET-WIRING.md.
#
# THE CHART REFUSES TO RENDER WITH PLACEHOLDER HOSTNAMES. templates/validate.yaml
# hard-fails on any `.invalid` domain and on a missing backstage.secretName, so
# a half-configured values.yaml is a render error on the controller, not a
# broken deployment on the cluster. Convenient, but it also means this path
# cannot be enabled "to see what happens".
#
# PREREQUISITES, all of which must be live before this path is enabled:
#   ../kgateway-crds, ../kgateway-params, ../kgateway  — the Gateway it renders
#   ../external-secrets, ../openbao, ../secret-store   — the backstage-secrets
#                                                        ExternalSecret
#   ../control-plane-extras                            — that ExternalSecret,
#                                                        plus the Certificate
#                                                        and Traefik Ingress
#   15-cert-manager + its letsencrypt-dns ClusterIssuer — TLS, and the
#                                                        self-signed Issuer
#                                                        chain for the
#                                                        cluster-gateway's
#                                                        internal mTLS
# Enable ../control-plane-extras FIRST. Backstage will not start without the
# Secret, and the chart will not render without `backstage.secretName` naming it.
#
# POST-INSTALL, AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL: the other three planes' agents verify
# this plane's cluster-gateway against a ConfigMap named `cluster-gateway-ca`
# that must exist in each of their namespaces. cert-manager mints that CA here,
# in this namespace, so it cannot be committed — it does not exist until this
# bundle has run. One command per plane namespace, in README.md under
# "Bootstrap: propagating the cluster-gateway CA". Until it is done, the data,
# workflow and observability planes come up but never register.
defaultNamespace: openchoreo-control-plane
helm:
  releaseName: openchoreo-control-plane
  chart: oci://ghcr.io/openchoreo/helm-charts/openchoreo-control-plane
  version: "1.2.1"
  valuesFiles:
    - values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true

# OpenChoreo control plane.
#
# Derived from the upstream single-cluster reference values
# (install/k3d/single-cluster/values-cp.yaml at release-v1.2), with three
# categories of change: real hostnames instead of `.localhost`, TLS moved to
# Traefik, and single-node scheduling fixes.
#
# ─── Hostnames and how traffic actually arrives ──────────────────────────────
# Public DNS (verified 2026-07-30):
#     openchoreo.ash4d.com      -> 192.168.7.150
#     api.openchoreo.ash4d.com  -> 192.168.7.150
#     thunder.ash4d.com         -> 192.168.7.150
# .150 is the Traefik LoadBalancer, so the path is
#
#     browser -> Traefik (TLS terminates here, ../control-plane-extras/)
#             -> gateway-default kgateway Service, ClusterIP
#             -> HTTPRoute host match -> openchoreo-api / backstage / thunder
#
# All three names are real public DNS records pointing at a LAN address, which
# is the same pattern every other ash4d.com service in this repo uses. That is
# also why the fixture credentials in ../thunder/values.yaml and
# ../openbao/values.yaml are tolerable: none of this is internet-reachable.
#
# Note thunder.ash4d.com is NOT under `.openchoreo.` — it is a sibling. The
# upstream file has thunder under the openchoreo subdomain; this deployment
# does not, because that is the record that already exists.

openchoreoApi:
  http:
    hostnames:
      - api.openchoreo.ash4d.com
  config:
    server:
      # Browser-facing, so https and no port — Traefik terminates on 443.
      # Upstream has http://...:8080 because k3d maps the gateway to a host
      # port. Getting this wrong does not break the API; it breaks the URLs
      # the API hands back to the CLI and the portal.
      publicUrl: "https://api.openchoreo.ash4d.com"

backstage:
