# Fleet bundle — control-plane TLS, Traefik ingress and Backstage secrets
# (raw manifests).
#
# The three things the control-plane chart cannot render for itself:
#
#   certificate.yaml    — one letsencrypt-dns Certificate covering all three
#                         control-plane hostnames
#   ingress.yaml        — the Traefik Ingress that terminates that TLS and
#                         forwards to the kgateway Gateway over ClusterIP
#   externalsecret.yaml — backstage-secrets, pulled from OpenBao via the
#                         `default` ClusterSecretStore
#
# Separate path from ../control-plane/ because Fleet allows one chart per
# path — the same split as 15-cert-manager/issuer and 18-lab-memory/raw.
#
# 🔴 ENABLE THIS BEFORE ../control-plane/, not after. The control-plane chart's
# validate.yaml fails the render outright when `backstage.secretName` is empty,
# and ../control-plane/values.yaml sets it to `backstage-secrets` — the Secret
# this bundle creates. Reversing the order does not break anything permanently
# (Backstage sits in CreateContainerConfigError until the Secret appears), but
# there is no reason to.
#
# ORDERING within its own prerequisites: needs ../external-secrets/ for the
# ExternalSecret CRD and ../secret-store/ for the store it names. Needs
# 15-cert-manager and its letsencrypt-dns ClusterIssuer for the Certificate.
# The Ingress can be applied before its backend Service exists — Traefik just
# 503s the route until the Gateway is provisioned — so nothing here has to
# wait on the chart.
defaultNamespace: openchoreo-control-plane

# Raw-manifest bundle, but Fleet still deploys it via Helm internally — so
# adopting objects that are already on the cluster needs takeOwnership. A
# no-op on first sync (nothing pre-exists); kept for convention and to protect
# a future re-adopt after a manual `kubectl apply`.
helm:
  takeOwnership: true

# TLS for every browser-facing control-plane hostname, in one Certificate.
#
# One cert with three SANs rather than three Certificates, because each
# Certificate is an independent DNS-01 round trip against the same zone and
# there is no reason to make cert-manager write three _acme-challenge records
# where one will do.
#
# thunder.ash4d.com rides along here even though Thunder itself runs in the
# `thunder` namespace: a Certificate's Secret is namespace-scoped, and the
# Ingress that consumes it (ingress.yaml) lives in THIS namespace because that
# is where the kgateway Gateway Service it forwards to lives. Thunder is
# reached through that same Gateway via its own HTTPRoute
# (../thunder/values.yaml), so one Ingress and one certificate cover all three.
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: openchoreo-ash4d-tls
  namespace: openchoreo-control-plane
spec:
  secretName: openchoreo-ash4d-tls
  # The cluster-scoped issuer from 15-cert-manager/issuer, DNS-01 via
  # Cloudflare. Cluster-scoped, so no per-namespace Issuer is needed here.
  issuerRef:
    kind: ClusterIssuer
    name: letsencrypt-dns
  dnsNames:
    - openchoreo.ash4d.com
    - api.openchoreo.ash4d.com
    - thunder.ash4d.com

input.content:
# Traefik ingress for the whole OpenChoreo control plane.
#
# ─── The two-hop path, and why it looks redundant ────────────────────────────
#     browser -> Traefik  (192.168.7.150, TLS terminates here)
#             -> gateway-default  (kgateway Envoy, ClusterIP)
#             -> HTTPRoute host match -> backstage / openchoreo-api / thunder
#
# Two proxies in a row is not an accident. OpenChoreo's charts only speak
# Gateway API — they render Gateways, HTTPRoutes and an HTTPListenerPolicy,
# and Thunder attaches its own HTTPRoute to `gateway-default` — so kgateway
# has to be the thing doing host and path routing. But every ash4d.com name in
# this cluster resolves to Traefik, and the DNS for these three already
# pointed there before this bundle existed. Fronting kgateway with Traefik
# means one LoadBalancer address instead of three (see ../kgateway-params/),
# and one TLS story shared with every other service in the repo.
#
# All three hosts route to the SAME backend Service on the SAME port. That is
# correct and not a copy-paste error: Traefik is doing nothing but TLS
# termination and forwarding here. The actual per-host dispatch happens one
# hop later, in kgateway, against the HTTPRoutes that the control-plane chart
# and Thunder create.
#
# ─── The backend Service name ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# `gateway-default` is the Service kgateway PROVISIONS for the Gateway object
# of the same name — it is created by the kgateway controller at runtime, not
# by any chart in this repo, so it will not exist until ../control-plane/ has
# been deployed and kgateway has reconciled its Gateway. Traefik returns 503
# for these hosts until then, which is the expected intermediate state and not
# a fault. Confirm the name on first deploy with
#
#     kubectl -n openchoreo-control-plane get svc,gateway
#
# and if kgateway ever changes its naming convention, this file is the single
# place that needs updating.
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: openchoreo
  namespace: openchoreo-control-plane
  annotations:
    # cert-manager's ingress-shim mints a Certificate from the tls block
    # below — one cert, three SANs, one DNS-01 round trip. Same convention as
    # 06-milvus/attu, 10-hermes and 21-unsloth-studio.
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-dns
spec:
  ingressClassName: traefik
  rules:
    # The developer portal (Backstage).
    - host: openchoreo.ash4d.com
      http:
        paths:
          - backend:
              service:
                name: gateway-default
                port:
                  number: 80
            path: /
            pathType: Prefix
    # The OpenChoreo API — also what the `openchoreo` CLI talks to.
    - host: api.openchoreo.ash4d.com
      http:
        paths:
          - backend:
              service:
                name: gateway-default
                port:
                  number: 80
            path: /
            pathType: Prefix
    # Thunder, the OIDC provider. It runs in the `thunder` namespace but
    # attaches its HTTPRoute to this namespace's Gateway
    # (../thunder/values.yaml, httproute.parentRefs), so it is reached through
    # the same Service — no second Ingress and no cross-namespace backend.
    - host: thunder.ash4d.com
      http:
        paths:
          - backend:
              service:
                name: gateway-default
                port:
                  number: 80
            path: /
            pathType: Prefix
  tls:
    # One secret for all three hosts. Keeping them in a single tls entry is
    # what makes the shim issue ONE Certificate with three SANs instead of
    # three separate DNS-01 challenges against the same zone.
    - hosts:
        - openchoreo.ash4d.com
        - api.openchoreo.ash4d.com
        - thunder.ash4d.com
      secretName: openchoreo-ash4d-tls

# Backstage's credentials, pulled from OpenBao through the `default`
# ClusterSecretStore (../secret-store/) into a Secret named
# `backstage-secrets` — the name ../control-plane/values.yaml sets as
# `backstage.secretName`, and which that chart's validate.yaml refuses to
# render without.
#
# ALL FIVE KEYS MUST RESOLVE OR THE ExternalSecret NEVER GOES READY, and
# Backstage stays in CreateContainerConfigError. Three of them are
# placeholders — ../control-plane/values.yaml leaves both external-CI
# integrations (Jenkins, GitHub Actions) disabled — but ExternalSecret treats
# a missing remoteRef as an error, not an omission, so all five are seeded in
# ../openbao/values.yaml regardless. If you ever trim this list, trim the
# OpenBao seeds to match, not the other way round.
#
# `backend-secret` signs Backstage's own sessions. `client-secret` is its OIDC
# confidential-client secret and MUST equal the openchoreo-backstage-client
# secret in ../thunder/values.yaml — see that file's header for why those
# values are literals in this repo.
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: backstage-secrets
  namespace: openchoreo-control-plane
spec:
  # OpenBao here is in-memory (../openbao/fleet.yaml), so it reseeds itself on
  # every restart with the same values — a 1h refresh is about re-reading
  # unchanged data, not about picking up rotations. After deliberately
  # changing a seed, delete this object rather than waiting the hour.
  refreshInterval: 1h
  secretStoreRef:
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
    name: default
  target:
    name: backstage-secrets
  data:
    - secretKey: backend-secret
      remoteRef: { key: backstage-backend-secret, property: value }
    - secretKey: client-secret
      remoteRef: { key: backstage-client-secret, property: value }
    - secretKey: jenkins-api-key
      remoteRef: { key: backstage-jenkins-api-key, property: value }
    - secretKey: github-actions-token
      remoteRef: { key: backstage-github-actions-token, property: value }
    - secretKey: github-oauth-client-secret
      remoteRef: { key: backstage-github-oauth-client-secret, property: value }

input.content:
# Fleet bundle — OpenChoreo data plane (Helm).
#
# Where deployed components actually run. Two pieces: a kgateway Gateway that
# fronts every workload OpenChoreo deploys, and `cluster-agent-dataplane`, a
# websocket client that dials the control plane's cluster-gateway over mTLS
# and is how this plane is driven.
#
# Chart 1.2.1, pinned to match ../control-plane/. The planes are versioned and
# released together; do not bump one without the other.
#
# On this single-node cluster the "data plane" is the same node as the control
# plane. That is the supported single-cluster topology (upstream's own
# install/k3d/single-cluster), not a compromise — the separation is by
# namespace and by agent, not by machine.
#
# 🔴 TWO PREREQUISITES THAT ARE NOT SATISFIED BY ENABLING PATHS IN ORDER:
#
# 1. The `cluster-gateway-ca` ConfigMap must exist in openchoreo-data-plane

# Fleet bundle — data-plane workload ingress (raw manifest).
#
# The Traefik Ingress and wildcard certificate for everything OpenChoreo
# deploys. Separate path from ../data-plane/ because Fleet allows one chart

#
# Checked 2026-07-30: NXDOMAIN. openchoreo.ash4d.com, api.openchoreo.ash4d.com
# and thunder.ash4d.com all resolve to .150; this one does not. Create it
# before enabling this path, or the certificate never issues — a DNS-01
# wildcard challenge writes `_acme-challenge.openchoreoapis.ash4d.com`, so
# cert-manager needs the zone, and Traefik needs the record to be reachable.
#
# Nothing else breaks while it is missing: the control plane, the portal and
# the CLI are all on the three names that already resolve. What you lose is
# the ability to reach a component you have deployed — which is most of the
# point of OpenChoreo, so treat this as required rather than optional.
#
# WHY A WILDCARD. OpenChoreo mints a hostname per component per environment,
# so the set is open-ended by design and cannot be enumerated in a repo. This
# is the one place in this cluster where a wildcard cert is the right answer
# rather than a shortcut.
defaultNamespace: openchoreo-data-plane

# Raw-manifest bundle, but Fleet still deploys it via Helm internally — so
# adopting objects that are already on the cluster needs takeOwnership. A
# no-op on first sync; kept for convention and to protect a future re-adopt
# after a manual `kubectl apply`.
helm:
  takeOwnership: true

# Traefik ingress for every component OpenChoreo deploys.
#
# Same two-hop shape as ../control-plane-extras/ingress.yaml — Traefik
# terminates TLS and forwards to a kgateway Gateway Service over ClusterIP,
# and kgateway does the real per-component routing against the HTTPRoutes the
# OpenChoreo controller creates as things are deployed.
#
# REQUIRES `*.openchoreoapis.ash4d.com  A  192.168.7.150`, which did not exist
# on 2026-07-30. See fleet.yaml.
#
# The backend Service `gateway-default` is provisioned by kgateway for the
# Gateway of the same name in this namespace, and does not exist until
# ../data-plane/ has been deployed. Traefik 503s until then — expected, not a
# fault. Verify the name on first deploy:
#
#     kubectl -n openchoreo-data-plane get svc,gateway
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: openchoreo-apis
  namespace: openchoreo-data-plane
  annotations:
    # ingress-shim issues the wildcard from the tls block below, DNS-01 via
    # Cloudflare. A wildcard is only possible with DNS-01, which is what
    # 15-cert-manager/issuer's letsencrypt-dns ClusterIssuer already does —
    # an HTTP-01 issuer could not serve this at all.
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-dns
spec:
  ingressClassName: traefik
  rules:
    # One wildcard rule. Individual component hostnames are created and
    # destroyed by OpenChoreo as components are deployed and removed, so
    # enumerating them here would mean editing this repo on every deploy —
    # exactly what the platform exists to avoid.
    - host: "*.openchoreoapis.ash4d.com"
      http:
        paths:
          - backend:
              service:
                name: gateway-default
                port:
                  number: 80
            path: /
            pathType: Prefix
  tls:
    - hosts:
        - "*.openchoreoapis.ash4d.com"
      secretName: openchoreoapis-ash4d-tls

# Fleet bundle — plane registration (raw manifests).
#
# Three cluster-scoped OpenChoreo objects — ClusterDataPlane,
# ClusterWorkflowPlane and ClusterObservabilityPlane — that tell the control
# plane the other three planes exist, and which CA to trust for each one's
# agent.
#
# A running cluster-agent is NOT a registered plane. The agent dials the
# control plane's cluster-gateway; these objects are the other half of that
# handshake. Without them the agents connect and are refused, and the portal
# shows no data plane to deploy to.
#
# ─── Why this is declarative at all ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Upstream's installer builds these imperatively — it waits for each plane's
# cert-manager Certificate, shells out for the CA, and inlines the PEM:
#
#     ca=$(kubectl get secret cluster-agent-tls -n $NS -o jsonpath=... | base64 -d)
#     ... clientCA: { value: | <pem> }
#
# which cannot be committed, because the PEM does not exist until the planes
# have run. The CRDs also accept `clientCA.secretKeyRef` with an explicit
# cross-namespace `namespace` field (confirmed against the v1.2.1 CRD schemas),
# so the same wiring can be expressed as a reference and shipped in git. That
# is what the manifests here do, and it is the reason plane registration is a
# Fleet path rather than another entry in the bootstrap section of README.md.
#
# ─── Ordering ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Needs the OpenChoreo CRDs from ../control-plane/, and each referenced
# `cluster-agent-tls` Secret only exists once that plane's chart has run and
# cert-manager has issued into it. Enable this LAST, after ../data-plane/,
# ../workflow-plane/ and ../observability-plane/.
#
# A registration whose Secret is not there yet is not fatal — the control
# plane reports the plane as not ready and reconciles when the Secret appears.
# But enabling this before the planes exist means three objects sitting in a
# failed state for no reason.
#
# 🔴 THESE ARE CLUSTER-SCOPED. Deleting this path deregisters all three planes
# at once, which is a platform-wide outage rather than a rollback of one thing.
defaultNamespace: openchoreo-control-plane

# Raw-manifest bundle, but Fleet still deploys it via Helm internally — so
# adopting objects that are already on the cluster needs takeOwnership. Not a
# no-op if these were ever created by hand from the upstream installer: with
# takeOwnership Fleet adopts them; without it the first sync fails on
# ownership.
helm:
  takeOwnership: true

# Registration of the three non-control planes with the control plane.
#
# Every `clientCA` below is a REFERENCE, not an inlined PEM. Upstream's
# installer shells out for each CA and pastes it in; the v1.2.1 CRDs also
# accept `secretKeyRef` with a cross-namespace `namespace`, which is what
# keeps this file committable. See fleet.yaml.
#
# The referenced Secret in each case is `cluster-agent-tls`, issued by
# cert-manager in that plane's own namespace because each plane chart sets
# `clusterAgent.tls.generateCerts: true`. The key is always `ca.crt`.
#
# `planeID: default` must match `clusterAgent.planeID` in the corresponding
# plane's values.yaml. They are joined by that string.

apiVersion: openchoreo.dev/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterDataPlane
metadata:
  name: default
spec:
  planeID: default
  clusterAgent:
    clientCA:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: cluster-agent-tls
        namespace: openchoreo-data-plane
        key: ca.crt
  # The ESO ClusterSecretStore deployed components resolve their secrets
  # through — ../secret-store/. Cluster-scoped, so the name alone is enough.
  secretStoreRef:
    name: default
  # Sends this plane's telemetry to the observability plane registered below.
  observabilityPlaneRef:
    kind: ClusterObservabilityPlane
    name: default
  gateway:
    ingress:
      external:
        # Identifies the Gateway OpenChoreo attaches component HTTPRoutes to.
        name: gateway-default
        namespace: openchoreo-data-plane
        http:
          # The suffix component hostnames are built from: a component in
          # project `p` environment `e` becomes something like
          # `<component>-<...>.openchoreoapis.ash4d.com`. This is what makes
          # the wildcard in ../data-plane-extras/ingress.yaml the right shape,
          # and why that DNS record is required rather than optional.
          host: openchoreoapis.ash4d.com
          # The listener on the Gateway object, named `http` by the data-plane
          # chart. Port 80 because ../data-plane/values.yaml puts the gateway
          # on standard ports; upstream's k3d values say 19080 for host-port
          # reasons that do not apply here.
          listenerName: http
          port: 80
---
apiVersion: openchoreo.dev/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterWorkflowPlane
metadata:
  name: default
spec:
  planeID: default
  clusterAgent:
    clientCA:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: cluster-agent-tls
        namespace: openchoreo-workflow-plane
        key: ca.crt
  # Builds write image-pull and registry credentials through the same store.
  # ../openbao/values.yaml's writer role deliberately binds
  # `openchoreo-workflow-plane` alongside `openbao` for exactly this.
  secretStoreRef:
    name: default
  observabilityPlaneRef:
    kind: ClusterObservabilityPlane
    name: default
---
apiVersion: openchoreo.dev/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterObservabilityPlane
metadata:
  name: default
spec:
  planeID: default
  clusterAgent:
    clientCA:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: cluster-agent-tls
        namespace: openchoreo-observability-plane
        key: ca.crt
  # In-cluster Service URL, not the public observer.openchoreo.ash4d.com name.
  # This is the control plane calling the observer server-side; routing it out
  # through Traefik and back would add a TLS hop and a dependency on public
  # DNS for a call that never leaves the node. The public name exists for the
  # browser (Backstage's observability tab) — see
  # ../observability-extras/ingress.yaml.
  observerURL: "http://observer.openchoreo-observability-plane.svc.cluster.local:8080"
  # rcaAgentURL and finOpsAgentURL are deliberately unset: both agents are
  # disabled in ../observability-plane/values.yaml (each wants an LLM endpoint
  # and ~1 GiB). Add them here when those are turned on.

# OpenChoreo workflow plane — Argo Workflows as OpenChoreo's build engine.
#
# Upstream's k3d values (install/k3d/single-cluster/values-wp.yaml) enable the
# Argo UI on a LoadBalancer at port 10081. That is dropped here: it would take
# one of the five remaining MetalLB addresses to expose a second, unauthenticated
# web UI for something the OpenChoreo portal already surfaces. Build status is
# visible in Backstage; `kubectl -n openchoreo-workflow-plane get workflows`
# covers the rest.

clusterAgent:
  # Must match `planeID` on the ClusterWorkflowPlane in ../registration/.
  planeID: default
  tls:
    generateCerts: true
    # 🔴 Not created by this chart — the control plane's cluster-gateway CA,
    # copied in by hand once. Missing it leaves this pod in
    # ContainerCreating. See README.md, "Bootstrap: propagating the
    # cluster-gateway CA".
    serverCAConfigMap: cluster-gateway-ca

argo-workflows:
  server:
    # No Argo UI. See the header — upstream turns this on for k3d
    # convenience; here it would cost a MetalLB address and add a second
    # unauthenticated console. The `authModes: [server]` upstream pairs it
    # with means no login at all, which is fine on a laptop and not here.
    enabled: false

  controller:
    # THE GUARDRAIL. Caps concurrent workflows on a node that is also running
    # LLM inference on a V100, milvus, and emby transcodes. Argo's default is
    # unlimited, which on a 16-thread box shared with those is how a build
    # storm becomes an inference outage.
    #
    # This limits workflow COUNT, not CPU — one buildpack build can still use
    # many cores. If builds interfere with anything else, drop this to 1
    # first; it is the cheapest lever here.
    parallelism: 2

    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 50m
        memory: 128Mi
      limits:
        cpu: 500m
        memory: 512Mi

    # Reap finished workflows rather than accumulating pods and their logs.
    # The node's containerd is shared with ~13 GB unsloth images and the
    # locally-built indexer images (08-indexer), so build leftovers are a real
    # disk concern, not a tidiness one.
    workflowDefaults:
      spec:
        ttlStrategy:
          secondsAfterCompletion: 3600
          secondsAfterSuccess: 3600
          secondsAfterFailure: 86400
        podGC:
          strategy: OnWorkflowCompletion

# Fleet bundle — build registry for the workflow plane (Helm).
#
# Where OpenChoreo pushes the images its builds produce, and where the data
# plane pulls them from. Plain `registry:2` via the twuni chart, which is what
# OpenChoreo's own single-cluster installer uses.
#
# ─── THIS CLUSTER ALREADY HAS A REGISTRY, AND THIS IS NOT IT ─────────────────
# Harbor runs at registry.ash4d.com in the `registry` namespace and already
# serves this cluster — 04-ollama/ollama-exporter pulls its image from there
# with the `harbor-pull` Secret. Using Harbor for OpenChoreo builds would be
# the better long-term answer: one registry, real authentication, scanning,
# retention.
#
# It is not what this bundle does, for reasons that are about this repo rather
# than about Harbor:
#
#   - Harbor is deliberately OUT of lab-fleet. FLEET-WIRING.md records why: its
#     objects are Helm-labelled but have no release Secret and no
#     meta.helm.sh/release-name, so the chart and values cannot be recovered
#     the way buzz's and openshell's were. Its install is unreconstructed.
#   - Wiring builds to it needs a robot account and a push Secret that exist
#     only on the cluster, so the interesting half of the configuration could
#     not live here anyway.
#   - A build pushing to Harbor on every commit changes the retention and disk
#     behaviour of a registry that is already load-bearing for the `ai`
#     namespace. That is a decision worth making deliberately, not as a side
#     effect of standing up OpenChoreo.
#
# So this is a small, isolated, throwaway registry whose blast radius is
# OpenChoreo alone. Switching to Harbor later is a change to the workflow
# templates' push target plus an imagePullSecret — this bundle can then be
# deleted outright, which is safe precisely because nothing else uses it.
#
# ClusterIP, unlike upstream's LoadBalancer on port 10082: k3d needs a host
# port, this cluster does not, and MetalLB's lan-pool had five free addresses.
# Nothing outside the cluster needs to reach this.
#
# 🔴 NO AUTHENTICATION. `registry:2` with no htpasswd, reachable by anything
# in the cluster that can resolve its Service. Acceptable only because it is
# ClusterIP-only and holds nothing but rebuildable build output. Do not expose
# it through Traefik, and do not start pushing anything to it you would mind
# another namespace reading.
defaultNamespace: openchoreo-workflow-plane
helm:
  releaseName: registry
  repo: https://twuni.github.io/docker-registry.helm
  chart: docker-registry
  version: "2.2.3"
  valuesFiles:
    - values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true

# Build registry for the OpenChoreo workflow plane.
#
# Derived from install/k3d/single-cluster/values-registry.yaml at
# release-v1.2, with the LoadBalancer dropped and storage made explicit.

# Upstream sets this so the Service is reachable as `registry` — workflow
# templates address it by that name. Keep it.

service:
  # Upstream uses `type: LoadBalancer, port: 10082` so a k3d host can docker
  # push into it. Nothing outside this cluster needs that, and MetalLB's
  # lan-pool had five free addresses when this was written. ClusterIP.
  type: ClusterIP
  port: 5000

persistence:
  enabled: true
  # Explicit, because this cluster has TWO default StorageClasses —
  # `local-path` and `longhorn` are both annotated
  # storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: true (observed 2026-07-30).
  # An unset storageClassName is therefore genuinely ambiguous here, not a
  # safe default. Longhorn so build output survives a node reboot the way
  # every other stateful workload in this repo does.
  storageClass: longhorn
  size: 20Gi

# Build output only. Nothing here cannot be rebuilt from source, so this is
# sized to hold a working set rather than a history — see the deleteEnabled
# note below.
deleteEnabled: true

# `registry:2` garbage collection is not automatic: deleting a manifest frees
# the tag, not the blobs. With deleteEnabled above, OpenChoreo can delete
# manifests, but blob storage still grows until a `registry garbage-collect`
# runs. On a 20Gi volume that is months away, not days — but it is the reason
# this claim will eventually need attention, and the reason it is 20Gi and not
# 5Gi. Longhorn supports online expansion if it fills.

resources:
  requests:
    cpu: 20m
    memory: 64Mi
  limits:
    cpu: 500m
    memory: 512Mi

# Fleet bundle — observability-plane secrets and ingress (raw manifests).
#
# Two ExternalSecrets and one Traefik Ingress:
#   externalsecrets.yaml — observer-secret and opensearch-admin-credentials
#   ingress.yaml         — observer.openchoreo.ash4d.com
#
# Separate path from ../observability-plane/ because Fleet allows one chart
# per path.
#
# 🔴 ENABLE THIS BEFORE ../observability-plane/. That chart hard-fails its
# render when `observer.secretName` is unset, and ../observability-plane/
# names `observer-secret` — the Secret this bundle materialises. The
# OpenSearch credentials are likewise consumed by ../observability-logs/,
# ../observability-traces/ and ../observability-events/, all of which reference
# `opensearch-admin-credentials` by name.
#
# 🔴 ingress.yaml NEEDS A DNS RECORD THAT DID NOT EXIST WHEN THIS WAS WRITTEN:
#
#     observer.openchoreo.ash4d.com   A   192.168.7.150
#
# Checked 2026-07-30: NXDOMAIN. Backstage's observability tab calls the
# observer FROM THE BROWSER, so this is not an internal-only URL — without the
# record, logs and traces in the portal fail with a CORS/DNS error while
# everything else works. The control plane's own server-side calls use the
# in-cluster Service URL instead (../registration/clusterplanes.yaml) and are
# unaffected.
#
# ORDERING: needs ../external-secrets/ and ../secret-store/ for the
# ExternalSecrets, and 15-cert-manager for the certificate. Nothing here waits
# on the observability chart itself.
defaultNamespace: openchoreo-observability-plane

# Raw-manifest bundle, but Fleet still deploys it via Helm internally — so
# adopting objects that are already on the cluster needs takeOwnership. A
# no-op on first sync; kept for convention.
helm:
  takeOwnership: true

# Observability-plane credentials, pulled from OpenBao through the `default`
# ClusterSecretStore (../secret-store/).

# The observer's OIDC client secret. Named by `observer.secretName` in
# ../observability-plane/values.yaml, whose chart REFUSES TO RENDER without
# it. The key name is fixed by the observer binary — it reads the env var
# UID_RESOLVER_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET directly, so `secretKey` here is not free
# to change.
#
# The value must equal the openchoreo-observer-resource-reader-client secret
# in ../thunder/values.yaml.
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: observer-secret
  namespace: openchoreo-observability-plane
spec:
  refreshInterval: 1h
  secretStoreRef:
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
    name: default
  target:
    name: observer-secret
  data:
    - secretKey: UID_RESOLVER_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
      remoteRef: { key: observer-oauth-client-secret, property: value }
---
# OpenSearch admin credentials, shared by four consumers:
#   ../observability-logs/    — OpenSearch itself, its setup Job, and fluent-bit
#   ../observability-traces/  — the tracing setup Job and OTel exporter
#   ../observability-events/  — the events OTel collector's basicauth extension
# All four reference this Secret BY NAME, so renaming it means editing all
# four values files.
#
# 🔴 THE PASSWORD IS WRITE-ONCE. OpenSearch seeds its internal security index
# from OPENSEARCH_INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD on FIRST START ONLY
# (../observability-logs/values.yaml). Changing the value in OpenBao later
# rotates what every client presents, but NOT what OpenSearch accepts — the
# result is a cluster nothing can authenticate to. Rotating it properly means
# an OpenSearch-side password change, or deleting its PVC and starting over.
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: opensearch-admin-credentials
  namespace: openchoreo-observability-plane
spec:
  refreshInterval: 1h
  secretStoreRef:
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
    name: default
  target:
    name: opensearch-admin-credentials
  data:
    - secretKey: username
      remoteRef: { key: opensearch-username, property: value }
    - secretKey: password
      remoteRef: { key: opensearch-password, property: value }

# Traefik ingress for the observer API.
#
# Same two-hop shape as the other two planes: Traefik terminates TLS and
# forwards to this namespace's kgateway Gateway Service over ClusterIP.
#
# WHY THIS HOSTNAME EXISTS AT ALL, given the control plane calls the observer
# over an in-cluster Service URL: Backstage's observability tab queries the
# observer FROM THE BROWSER. That is also why
# ../observability-plane/values.yaml sets `observer.cors.allowedOrigins` to
# https://openchoreo.ash4d.com — a same-node Service URL is not reachable from
# a laptop, so the browser needs a public name and the observer needs to
# accept the portal's origin.
#
# 🔴 REQUIRES `observer.openchoreo.ash4d.com  A  192.168.7.150`, which was
# NXDOMAIN on 2026-07-30. Without it: the portal renders, and its logs and
# traces panels fail. Everything else is unaffected.
#
# Backend `gateway-default` is provisioned by kgateway for this namespace's
# Gateway and does not exist until ../observability-plane/ has deployed.
# Traefik 503s until then.
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: observer
  namespace: openchoreo-observability-plane
  annotations:
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-dns
spec:
  ingressClassName: traefik
  rules:
    - host: observer.openchoreo.ash4d.com
      http:
        paths:
          - backend:
              service:
                name: gateway-default
                port:
                  number: 80
            path: /
            pathType: Prefix
  tls:
    - hosts:
        - observer.openchoreo.ash4d.com
      secretName: observer-ash4d-tls

# Fleet bundle — OpenChoreo observability plane (Helm).
#
# The query layer: the `observer` API that Backstage's logs, traces, metrics
# and alerts panels talk to, plus a controller-manager and
# `cluster-agent-observabilityplane`. It stores nothing itself — the actual
# telemetry backends are the four sibling module bundles:
#
#   ../observability-logs     OpenSearch + fluent-bit   (container logs)
#   ../observability-traces   OTel collector -> OpenSearch (traces)
#   ../observability-metrics  PrometheusAgent           (metrics)
#   ../observability-events   OTel collector -> OpenSearch (k8s events)
#
# Chart 1.2.1, pinned to match the other planes.
#
# ─── This is the heaviest thing in 22-openchoreo ─────────────────────────────
# The observer itself is small. OpenSearch is not. When this scope was chosen,
# sdf1 was at 74% memory (48 GiB of 64 GiB) with ollama, milvus, comfyui,
# emby and the k3s control plane resident. Budget roughly 2-3 GiB for the
# OpenSearch instance in ../observability-logs plus the collectors, on top of
# ~1 GiB for the plane itself.
#
# Enable the four module bundles ONE AT A TIME and watch `kubectl top node`
# between each. If memory becomes a problem, ../observability-metrics is the
# cheapest to drop (Rancher's Prometheus already scrapes this cluster) and
# ../observability-traces the next (it reuses the logs OpenSearch but adds a
# tail-sampling collector).
#
# PREREQUISITES:
#   ../observability-extras — the observer-secret ExternalSecret. The chart
#                             REFUSES TO RENDER without observer.secretName,
#                             so enable that path first.
#   the `cluster-gateway-ca` ConfigMap in openchoreo-observability-plane —
#                             same manual copy as the other planes, README.md.
#   ../registration         — the ClusterObservabilityPlane. Enable last.
#
# The chart also brings a CRD (ObservabilityAlertsNotificationChannel), so the
# usual rule applies: pause the GitRepo to roll back, do not remove the path.
defaultNamespace: openchoreo-observability-plane
helm:
  releaseName: openchoreo-observability-plane
  chart: oci://ghcr.io/openchoreo/helm-charts/openchoreo-observability-plane
  version: "1.2.1"
  valuesFiles:
    - values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true

# OpenChoreo observability plane — the observer API behind Backstage's logs,
# traces, metrics and alerts panels.
#
# Derived from install/k3d/single-cluster/values-op.yaml at release-v1.2.

observer:
  # Materialised by ../observability-extras/externalsecrets.yaml. The chart's
  # validate hard-fails if this is empty, so that path must be enabled first.
  secretName: observer-secret

  # Server-side call from the observer to the control plane's API. In-cluster
  # Service URL rather than https://api.openchoreo.ash4d.com: routing a
  # same-node call out through Traefik and back adds a TLS hop and makes an
  # internal control path depend on public DNS. Upstream uses the public name
  # only because k3d has no other option.
  controlPlaneApiUrl: "http://openchoreo-api.openchoreo-control-plane.svc.cluster.local:8080"

  # Backstage queries the observer FROM THE BROWSER, so the portal's public
  # origin has to be allowed explicitly. This must match
  # `backstage.baseUrl` in ../control-plane/values.yaml exactly — an origin
  # comparison is a string comparison, and a mismatch shows up as empty
  # panels with a CORS error in the console rather than as anything that
  # names this file.
  cors:
    allowedOrigins:
      - "https://openchoreo.ash4d.com"

  extraEnvs:
    # The observer's own public base URL, used to build links it hands back.
    # Browser-facing, so the Traefik name — see
    # ../observability-extras/ingress.yaml, and note that record did not
    # exist on 2026-07-30.
    - name: OBSERVER_BASE_URL
      value: "https://observer.openchoreo.ash4d.com"
    - name: AUTHZ_TIMEOUT
      value: "30s"

  http:
    hostnames:
      - observer.openchoreo.ash4d.com

  # Alerts in SQLite, in-pod, no PVC — matching upstream. Alert state is
  # derived from telemetry that lives in OpenSearch, so a restart costs
  # suppression windows rather than data. The alternative backend is
  # postgresql, which would mean running a database for this alone.
  alertStoreBackend: sqlite

security:
  oidc:
    # In-cluster Service URLs, deliberately, and NOT https://thunder.ash4d.com.
    # This is the observer validating tokens server-side on every request; the
    # public name would route it through Traefik and make token validation
    # depend on public DNS and a certificate. Note the port is 8090 —
    # Thunder's own listener — not the 443 the browser uses.
    jwksUrl: "http://thunder-service.thunder.svc.cluster.local:8090/oauth2/jwks"
    tokenUrl: "http://thunder-service.thunder.svc.cluster.local:8090/oauth2/token"
    # This one IS the public name: it goes into OAuth metadata the browser
    # reads, so it has to be an address the browser can reach.
    authServerBaseUrl: "https://thunder.ash4d.com"

clusterAgent:
  # Must match `planeID` on the ClusterObservabilityPlane in ../registration/.
  planeID: default
  tls:
    generateCerts: true
    # 🔴 Not created by this chart — copied in by hand once from the control
    # plane. See README.md, "Bootstrap: propagating the cluster-gateway CA".
    serverCAConfigMap: cluster-gateway-ca

gateway:
  # Standard ports behind Traefik, unlike upstream's 11080/11085 (k3d host
  # ports). TLS terminates at Traefik — see ../observability-extras/ingress.yaml.
  httpPort: 80
  httpsPort: 443
  tls:
    enabled: false

# ─── Both AI agents are off ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The RCA (root-cause analysis) and FinOps agents each want an LLM endpoint
# and each request ~1 GiB with a 1.5 GiB limit — 3 GiB of the node's remaining
# headroom between them, for features that do nothing without a model.
#
# Their OAuth client secrets ARE already seeded in ../openbao/values.yaml and
# their Thunder clients already exist, so enabling either later is a values
# change here plus an LLM endpoint — no credential work. The lab's ollama
# proxy at ollama-exporter.ai.svc.cluster.local:9401 is the obvious candidate
# for `llm.baseUrl`, which would also mean the V100 gets pulled into serving
# these; that is a deliberate decision, not a default.
#
# If either is turned on, add its URL to the ClusterObservabilityPlane in
# ../registration/ (`rcaAgentURL` / `finOpsAgentURL`) or the control plane
# will not route to it.
rca:
  enabled: false
finOpsAgent:
  enabled: false

# Fleet bundle — container logs: OpenSearch + fluent-bit (Helm).
#
# OpenChoreo's log backend. Three pieces from one chart: an OpenSearch
# instance, a fluent-bit DaemonSet tailing container logs into it, and an
# adapter the observer queries.
#
# Chart 0.5.3 — the version OpenChoreo v1.2's installer pins. Note the
# observability MODULES are versioned INDEPENDENTLY of the planes: this is
# 0.5.3 while the planes are 1.2.1. That is upstream's scheme, not a mistake,
# and it means bumping the planes does not imply bumping these.
#
# 🔴 THE HEAVIEST BUNDLE IN 22-openchoreo, AND THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO HURT.
# OpenSearch is a JVM with a persistent volume. Budget ~1.5-2 GiB resident on
# a node that was at 74% memory (48 GiB of 64 GiB) when this was written.
# Enable it on its own and watch `kubectl top node` before enabling any other
# observability module.
#
# ENABLE THIS BEFORE ../observability-traces/ and ../observability-events/.
# Both write into THIS OpenSearch rather than running their own — traces sets
# `openSearch.enabled: false` precisely so there is one instance, not three.
# Enabling either first leaves it with nowhere to write.
#
# PREREQUISITE: the `opensearch-admin-credentials` Secret from
# ../observability-extras/. Referenced by name three times in values.yaml.
#
# 🔴 fluent-bit NEEDS /etc/machine-id ON THE NODE. Upstream's k3d installer
# patches this in because k3d containers lack it:
#
#     [ -s /etc/machine-id ] || uuid | tr -d '-' > /etc/machine-id
#
# sdf1 is a real openSUSE Leap host, so systemd has always populated it and no
# patch is needed. Verify once before enabling — `cat /etc/machine-id` on the
# node — because an empty file makes every fluent-bit pod crashloop with an
# error that does not mention machine-id.
defaultNamespace: openchoreo-observability-plane
helm:
  releaseName: observability-logs-opensearch
  chart: oci://ghcr.io/openchoreo/helm-charts/observability-logs-opensearch
  version: "0.5.3"
  valuesFiles:
    - values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true

input.content:
# Container logs — OpenSearch, fluent-bit and the observer's log adapter.
#
# Upstream's installer passes only the two secret-name flags and then does a
# second `helm upgrade --reuse-values --set fluent-bit.enabled=true` to turn
# fluent-bit on after OpenSearch is up. That two-pass dance exists because the
# installer is a shell script; Fleet reconciles continuously, so fluent-bit is
# simply enabled here and retries until OpenSearch answers.

# Referenced by name from ../observability-extras/externalsecrets.yaml. Both
# the setup Job and the query adapter authenticate with it.
openSearchSetup:
  openSearchSecretName: opensearch-admin-credentials
  dataRetentionTime:
    # 30d is upstream's default and it is a real disk commitment on a shared
    # Longhorn pool (428 GiB available of 1049 GiB on 2026-07-30). Cut to 7d:
    # this is a lab whose logs are for debugging a deploy that just happened,
    # not for compliance. Raising it later is a values change; recovering the
    # disk after it fills is not.
    containerLogs: 7d
    k8sEvents: 7d

adapter:
  openSearchSecretName: opensearch-admin-credentials

openSearch:
  # ONE node, not the subchart's default of three. `singleNode: true` is
  # already upstream's setting here and it is load-bearing on this cluster:
  # three OpenSearch replicas on one Kubernetes node would be three JVMs
  # competing for the same RAM to provide redundancy that a single node cannot
  # deliver anyway.
  singleNode: true
  replicas: 1

  # 🔴 SEEDS THE SECURITY INDEX ON FIRST START ONLY. This value must equal the
  # `opensearch-password` seed in ../openbao/values.yaml, which is what
  # ../observability-extras/ hands to every client. Changing it later does NOT
  # change what OpenSearch accepts — see the warning in that file. This is an
  # upstream fixture credential; the same reasoning as ../thunder/values.yaml
  # applies (LAN-only, rotate deliberately, README.md).
  extraEnvs:
    - name: OPENSEARCH_INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD
      value: ThisIsTheOpenSearchPassword1

  # The subchart requests 1000m CPU and no memory at all by default. On a
  # 16-thread node already at ~50% CPU requests that single request is 6% of
  # the box reserved for an idle JVM, and the missing memory request means the
  # scheduler cannot account for the largest consumer here. Both corrected.
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 1Gi
    limits:
      cpu: 2000m
      memory: 2Gi

  # Heap. The subchart default is -Xmx512M, which is fine for the volume this
  # lab produces and deliberately left well under the 2Gi limit — OpenSearch
  # needs off-heap room for Lucene, and a heap sized close to the container
  # limit is the classic way to get OOMKilled instead of GC pressure.
  opensearchJavaOpts: "-Xmx512M -Xms512M"

  persistence:
    enabled: true
    # Explicit because this cluster has TWO default StorageClasses —
    # `local-path` and `longhorn` are both marked default (observed
    # 2026-07-30) — so an unset class is genuinely ambiguous here.
    storageClass: longhorn
    # 8Gi is the subchart default and is right for 7d retention at lab volume.
    # Longhorn expands online if it turns out not to be.
    size: 8Gi

fluent-bit:
  # On, in one pass — see the header. Tails every container on the node, so
  # this is also the component that makes OpenChoreo's log panels show logs
  # from workloads that have nothing to do with OpenChoreo.
  enabled: true
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 25m
      memory: 128Mi
    limits:
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 256Mi

# Fleet bundle — metrics: Prometheus for OpenChoreo (Helm).
#
# Chart 0.6.1 — OpenChoreo v1.2's installer pin. Bundles
# kube-prometheus-stack 81.6.3 (prometheus-operator v0.88.1) as a subchart,
# plus a metrics adapter the observer queries and an Alertmanager route that
# webhooks OpenChoreo's alerts back into that adapter.
#
# 🔴 THE HIGHEST-RISK PATH IN 22-openchoreo. ENABLE IT LAST, ON ITS OWN, AND
# BE WILLING TO DROP IT.
#
# ─── The collision ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# THIS CLUSTER ALREADY RUNS kube-prometheus-stack. `rancher-monitoring`
# (rancher-monitoring-109.0.2+up80.9.1, prometheus-operator v0.87.1) lives in
# cattle-monitoring-system, its CRDs are owned by the separate
# `rancher-monitoring-crd` release, and 03-gpu/dcgm-exporter already feeds it.
# Installed with upstream's defaults, this chart would:
#
#   1. claim the ten monitoring.coreos.com CRDs that rancher-monitoring-crd
#      owns — two Helm releases, one set of cluster-scoped objects; and
#   2. run a SECOND prometheus-operator. Rancher's has no --namespaces
#      restriction (verified 2026-07-30), so both would reconcile every
#      Prometheus, Alertmanager and ServiceMonitor in the cluster, at two
#      different operator versions, rewriting each other's StatefulSets.
#
# That is the `03-gpu/runtimeclass` failure mode with Rancher's monitoring
# stack as the blast radius. values.yaml therefore disables both the CRDs and
# the bundled operator, and lets RANCHER's operator reconcile the Prometheus
# and Alertmanager objects this chart declares. One operator, two Prometheus
# instances.
#
# ─── The residual risk, stated plainly ───────────────────────────────────────
# That leaves a version skew: the chart is built for operator v0.88.1 and
# Rancher's CRDs are v0.87.1. Defaults do not appear to use v0.88-only fields,
# so it should apply — but "should" is doing real work in that sentence, and
# this is the one bundle here whose failure mode reaches OUTSIDE OpenChoreo.
# Verify before trusting it:
#
#     kubectl -n openchoreo-observability-plane get prometheus,alertmanager
#     kubectl -n cattle-monitoring-system get prometheus,statefulset   # unchanged?
#     kubectl -n cattle-monitoring-system logs deploy/rancher-monitoring-operator --tail=50
#
# If Rancher's own Prometheus StatefulSet churns, or its operator logs errors
# about OpenChoreo's objects, remove this path immediately — it is a raw
# Helm release Fleet created itself, with no adopted state, so removing it is
# safe here (the FLEET-WIRING.md warning about path removal applies to bundles
# that took ownership of a PRE-EXISTING release; this is not one).
#
# ─── It is also the most droppable ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Without it: Backstage's logs and traces panels still work
# (../observability-logs/, ../observability-traces/); the metrics panels are
# empty. Rancher's Grafana at 192.168.7.152 still shows everything it always
# did, including GPU metrics. On a node that was at 74% memory when this was
# written, running a second cluster-wide Prometheus for one portal tab is a
# defensible thing to say no to.
defaultNamespace: openchoreo-observability-plane
helm:
  releaseName: observability-metrics-prometheus
  chart: oci://ghcr.io/openchoreo/helm-charts/observability-metrics-prometheus
  version: "0.6.1"
  valuesFiles:
    - values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true

# Metrics for OpenChoreo, coexisting with Rancher's monitoring stack.
#
# Read ../observability-metrics/fleet.yaml first. Every override below exists
# because this cluster already runs kube-prometheus-stack as
# `rancher-monitoring` in cattle-monitoring-system, and the chart's defaults
# assume it is the only one.
#
# The adapter hardcodes its backend as
#   http://openchoreo-observability-prometheus.<namespace>:9091
# (templates/adapter/configmap.yaml — not a value), which is why the
# Prometheus below must keep the chart's `fullnameOverride: openchoreo-
# observability` and its port 9091. Do not rename either.

kube-prometheus-stack:
  # Keep the subchart: it declares the Prometheus and Alertmanager objects
  # OpenChoreo needs. What is disabled below is the machinery that would
  # duplicate Rancher's.
  enabled: true

  # 🔴 THE TWO LINES THAT PREVENT A CLUSTER-WIDE COLLISION.
  #
  # CRDs: all ten monitoring.coreos.com CRDs are already on the cluster, owned
  # by the `rancher-monitoring-crd` Helm release. Leaving this true means two
  # releases claiming the same cluster-scoped objects — and a future `helm
  # uninstall` of either taking Rancher's monitoring with it.
  crds:
    enabled: false

  # Operator: Rancher's prometheus-operator v0.87.1 watches ALL namespaces (no
  # --namespaces argument, verified 2026-07-30), so it will reconcile the
  # Prometheus and Alertmanager declared here without a second operator
  # existing. Two operators at different versions would fight over every
  # Prometheus CR in the cluster, Rancher's included.
  prometheusOperator:
    enabled: false

  prometheus:
    enabled: true
    service:
      # Chart default is LoadBalancer, which would take one of the five
      # remaining MetalLB addresses in lan-pool to expose a Prometheus that
      # only the in-cluster adapter talks to.
      type: ClusterIP
      # Must stay 9091 — the adapter's hardcoded backend port. See header.
      port: 9091
    prometheusSpec:
      # This instance scrapes every ServiceMonitor in every namespace
      # (serviceMonitorSelector: {} in the chart's own values), which means it
      # duplicates Rancher's entire scrape workload. That is what makes
      # OpenChoreo's metrics panels work, and it is also the main reason this
      # bundle is expensive. Retention is therefore deliberately short —
      # Rancher's Prometheus remains the long-term store for anything that is
      # not an OpenChoreo panel.
      retention: 3d
      retentionSize: 4GB
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu: 100m
          memory: 512Mi
        limits:
          cpu: 1000m
          memory: 2Gi
      storageSpec:
        volumeClaimTemplate:
          spec:
            # Explicit: this cluster has TWO default StorageClasses
            # (local-path and longhorn are both marked default, observed
            # 2026-07-30), so an unset class is ambiguous.
            storageClassName: longhorn
            accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
            resources:
              requests:
                storage: 6Gi

  # Kept — small, and it is what routes OpenChoreo's alerts to the metrics
  # adapter's webhook (the `openchoreo-alerts` receiver in the chart's own
  # values). Rancher's Alertmanager serves a different purpose and neither
  # knows about the other.
  alertmanager:
    enabled: true

  # Rancher already runs kube-state-metrics, and this Prometheus scrapes every
  # ServiceMonitor in the cluster — including Rancher's KSM one. A second
  # instance would double the memory to produce identical series.
  kubeStateMetrics:
    enabled: false

  # Same reasoning: Rancher already ships ServiceMonitors for the kubelet and
  # friends, and this Prometheus picks them up cluster-wide. Declaring a
  # second set would mean two ServiceMonitors per target, scraped by both
  # Prometheus instances.
  kubernetesServiceMonitors:
    enabled: false
  kubelet:
    enabled: false

  # Off in the chart's defaults already, restated because a second Grafana
  # would be actively confusing next to Rancher's at 192.168.7.152.
  grafana:
    enabled: false

# Fleet bundle — Kubernetes events into OpenSearch (Helm).
#
# An OpenTelemetry collector that watches Kubernetes Events and writes them to
# the `k8s-events` index in the OpenSearch that ../observability-logs/ runs.
# This is what puts "why is my pod not starting" into the OpenChoreo portal
# next to the container logs.
#
# Chart 0.1.1 — OpenChoreo v1.2's installer pin, and the youngest chart in
# this bundle by some margin. Versioned independently of the planes.
#
# REQUIRES ../observability-logs/ TO BE LIVE FIRST — it writes into that
# OpenSearch and brings none of its own.
#
# PREREQUISITE: `opensearch-admin-credentials` from ../observability-extras/.
#
# The lightest of the four observability modules: one small collector, no
# storage, no JVM. If the node is tight, this is the last one to drop rather
# than the first.
#
# The exporter and basicauth wiring in values.yaml is verbatim from upstream's
# installer, which passes it as an inline `-f -` heredoc rather than shipping
# a values file. It is reproduced here so the configuration is reviewable in
# git instead of living in a shell script nobody runs.
defaultNamespace: openchoreo-observability-plane
helm:
  releaseName: observability-events-otel-collector
  chart: oci://ghcr.io/openchoreo/helm-charts/observability-events-otel-collector
  version: "0.1.1"
  valuesFiles:
    - values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true

# Kubernetes events -> OpenSearch, via an OpenTelemetry collector.
#
# Reproduced from the inline heredoc in OpenChoreo v1.2's installer
# (install/k3d/k3d-install.sh, install_observability_plane), so that this
# configuration is reviewable in git rather than embedded in a shell script.
# Only the resources block below is an addition.

collector:
  replicaCount: 1

  # Credentials for the OpenSearch that ../observability-logs/ runs, from the
  # shared Secret in ../observability-extras/externalsecrets.yaml. Injected as
  # env vars because the basicauth extension below interpolates them with
  # ${env:...} — the collector config is a ConfigMap, so the password must not
  # be written into it directly.
  extraEnv:
    - name: OPENSEARCH_USERNAME
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: opensearch-admin-credentials
          key: username
    - name: OPENSEARCH_PASSWORD
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: opensearch-admin-credentials
          key: password

  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 50m
      memory: 128Mi
    limits:
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 512Mi

extraExtensions:
  basicauth/opensearch:
    client_auth:
      username: ${env:OPENSEARCH_USERNAME}
      password: ${env:OPENSEARCH_PASSWORD}

exporters:
  opensearch:
    # A dedicated index, separate from container logs, with a daily rollover.
    # Retention for this index is governed by
    # ../observability-logs/values.yaml's `openSearchSetup.dataRetentionTime.
    # k8sEvents`, which is set to 7d there — the setting lives with the
    # OpenSearch that owns the index, not here.
    logs_index: "k8s-events"
    logs_index_time_format: "yyyy-MM-dd"

# 22 — OpenChoreo [OpenChoreo](https://openchoreo.dev) v1.2.1 — an open-source internal developer platform: a Backstage portal, a CRD-driven control plane, in-cluster builds, and logs/traces/metrics, deployed as **20 Fleet paths** across seven namespaces. This is the largest bundle in the repo, and the only one that is a whole platform rather than an application. It is also a **fresh install, not an adoption** — nothing here existed on the cluster beforehand, so Fleet deploys the moment a path lands. | | | |---|---| | Portal | [openchoreo.ash4d.com](https://openchoreo.ash4d.com) (Backstage) | | API / CLI | [api.openchoreo.ash4d.com](https://api.openchoreo.ash4d.com) | | Identity | [thunder.ash4d.com](https://thunder.ash4d.com) (ThunderID, OIDC) | | Observer | `observer.openchoreo.ash4d.com` — **DNS record not yet created** | | Workloads | `*.openchoreoapis.ash4d.com` — **DNS record not yet created** | ## Architecture on one node OpenChoreo is designed as four planes across as many clusters. This is the supported **single-cluster** topology: four planes, one node, separated by namespace and by agent rather than by machine. ```mermaid flowchart TD BROWSER([browser / CLI]) --> TRAEFIK[Traefik 192.168.7.150
TLS terminates here] subgraph cp["openchoreo-control-plane"] GWCP[gateway-default
kgateway, ClusterIP] API[openchoreo-api] BS[Backstage portal] CGW[cluster-gateway
mTLS hub] CTRL[controller-manager
36 CRDs] end subgraph th["thunder"] THUNDER[ThunderID
OIDC] end subgraph dp["openchoreo-data-plane"] GWDP[gateway-default] --> WL[deployed components] AGDP[cluster-agent] end subgraph wp["openchoreo-workflow-plane"] ARGO[Argo Workflows] --> REG[(registry)] AGWP[cluster-agent] end subgraph op["openchoreo-observability-plane"] OBS[observer API] OS[(OpenSearch
logs + traces)] PROM[Prometheus] AGOP[cluster-agent] end subgraph sec["external-secrets + openbao"] ESO[ESO] --> BAO[(OpenBao
dev mode)] end TRAEFIK --> GWCP --> API & BS TRAEFIK --> GWDP GWCP --> THUNDER BS -.OIDC.-> THUNDER CGW <-.mTLS.-> AGDP & AGWP & AGOP OBS --> OS & PROM BS -.->|browser| OBS ESO -.credentials.-> BS & OBS & OS classDef plane fill:#059669,stroke:#047857,color:#fff class API,BS,CGW,CTRL,GWCP plane ``` **Every hostname terminates at Traefik, not at a kgateway LoadBalancer.** The OpenChoreo charts only speak Gateway API, so kgateway has to do the host routing — but MetalLB's `lan-pool` had five free addresses when this was written, and giving each plane's Gateway one would have taken three of them for no benefit. `kgateway-params/` forces every Gateway Service to ClusterIP and Traefik fronts all of them. That is the single biggest deviation from upstream's install and the reason several values files disagree with the upstream reference. ## Install order Paths are added to the `lab-openchoreo` GitRepo **one at a time**, in this order. Nothing here is an adoption, so each path deploys as soon as it lands. | # | Path | Namespace | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | `22-openchoreo/external-secrets` | `external-secrets` | owns CRDs | | 2 | `22-openchoreo/openbao` | `openbao` | dev mode — read its `fleet.yaml` | | 3 | `22-openchoreo/secret-store` | `openbao` | needs 1 + 2 live | | 4 | `22-openchoreo/kgateway-crds` | `openchoreo-control-plane` | owns CRDs | | 5 | `22-openchoreo/kgateway-params` | `openchoreo-control-plane` | before 6 | | 6 | `22-openchoreo/kgateway` | `openchoreo-control-plane` | | | 7 | `22-openchoreo/control-plane-extras` | `openchoreo-control-plane` | **before 8** | | 8 | `22-openchoreo/control-plane` | `openchoreo-control-plane` | owns 36 CRDs | | — | *bootstrap: copy the cluster-gateway CA* | | **see below** | | 9 | `22-openchoreo/thunder` | `thunder` | after the CP Gateway exists | | 10 | `22-openchoreo/data-plane` | `openchoreo-data-plane` | | | 11 | `22-openchoreo/data-plane-extras` | `openchoreo-data-plane` | needs a DNS record | | 12 | `22-openchoreo/workflow-registry` | `openchoreo-workflow-plane` | before 13 | | 13 | `22-openchoreo/workflow-plane` | `openchoreo-workflow-plane` | build load — see its `fleet.yaml` | | 14 | `22-openchoreo/observability-extras` | `openchoreo-observability-plane` | **before 15** | | 15 | `22-openchoreo/observability-plane` | `openchoreo-observability-plane` | | | 16 | `22-openchoreo/observability-logs` | `openchoreo-observability-plane` | OpenSearch — heaviest | | 17 | `22-openchoreo/observability-traces` | `openchoreo-observability-plane` | needs 16 | | 18 | `22-openchoreo/observability-events` | `openchoreo-observability-plane` | needs 16 | | 19 | `22-openchoreo/observability-metrics` | `openchoreo-observability-plane` | **riskiest — see its `fleet.yaml`** | | 20 | `22-openchoreo/registration` | cluster-scoped | **last** | Three orderings are hard rather than preferences: - **`control-plane-extras` before `control-plane`**, and **`observability-extras` before `observability-plane`**. Both charts hard-fail their *render* when `backstage.secretName` / `observer.secretName` is empty, and those Secrets come from the `-extras` bundles. The failure is on the Fleet controller, not the cluster. - **`observability-logs` before `traces` and `events`.** Both write into the OpenSearch that `observability-logs` runs and bring none of their own. - **`registration` last.** It references a `cluster-agent-tls` Secret in each plane's namespace, which does not exist until that plane's chart has run. ### There is no `22-openchoreo` path Every path above is listed individually and `22-openchoreo` itself is **never** in `spec.paths`. That is deliberate: FLEET-WIRING.md records that a nested `fleet.yaml` deploys as soon as its *parent* path is adopted, so adding the parent here would deploy all twenty bundles at once — the opposite of a staged rollout. The directory has no `fleet.yaml` of its own precisely so that cannot happen by accident. ## Prerequisites ### Already satisfied on this cluster - **Gateway API v1.5.1, standard channel** — exactly what OpenChoreo v1.2 wants. **Do not run upstream's `kubectl apply .../standard-install.yaml` step.** These CRDs are owned by the k3s-bundled `traefik-crd` release in `kube-system` with `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep`. Reinstalling them aims Fleet at k3s's own objects — the `03-gpu/runtimeclass` failure mode, with every Ingress in the cluster as the blast radius. - **cert-manager v1.20.2 + the `letsencrypt-dns` ClusterIssuer** (15). Newer than the v1.19.4 upstream pins. Issues all three Ingress certificates and the internal CAs the plane agents use for mTLS. - **Longhorn** — 428 GiB available of 1049 GiB (2026-07-30). This bundle claims ~34 GiB: OpenSearch 8Gi, Prometheus 6Gi, registry 20Gi. > ⚠️ **Two default StorageClasses.** `local-path` and `longhorn` are *both* > annotated `storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: true`. An unset > `storageClassName` is therefore genuinely ambiguous on this cluster, which > is why every PVC in this bundle names `longhorn` explicitly. Worth fixing at > the cluster level, separately from OpenChoreo. ### Must be created before enabling the paths that need them **Two DNS records** (both were `NXDOMAIN` on 2026-07-30): ``` observer.openchoreo.ash4d.com A 192.168.7.150 # needed by path 14 *.openchoreoapis.ash4d.com A 192.168.7.150 # needed by path 11 ``` The three that already exist — `openchoreo.ash4d.com`, `api.openchoreo.ash4d.com`, `thunder.ash4d.com` — cover the portal, the API and login, so paths 1–10 work without either record. - Without the **observer** record: the portal works, its logs/traces/metrics tabs fail. Backstage queries the observer *from the browser*, so an in-cluster URL cannot substitute. - Without the **`*.openchoreoapis`** wildcard: you can build and deploy a component but not reach it. The wildcard is required because OpenChoreo mints a hostname per component per environment — the set cannot be enumerated in a repo. A wildcard needs DNS-01, which `letsencrypt-dns` already does. **No hand-created Secrets.** Unlike every other bundle in this repo, there is nothing to `kubectl create secret` — OpenBao seeds itself and ESO materialises the rest. See "Credentials" below for the tradeoff that buys. ## Bootstrap: propagating the cluster-gateway CA **The one manual step, and the most likely thing to go wrong.** Each plane's `cluster-agent` verifies the control plane's `cluster-gateway` against a ConfigMap named `cluster-gateway-ca` **in its own namespace**. The CA is minted by cert-manager in `openchoreo-control-plane` and does not exist until path 8 has run — so it cannot be committed here. Run this once, after path 8 and before the plane agents start (paths 10, 13, 15): ```bash CA=$(kubectl -n openchoreo-control-plane get secret cluster-gateway-ca \ -o jsonpath='{.data.ca\.crt}' | base64 -d) for ns in openchoreo-data-plane openchoreo-workflow-plane openchoreo-observability-plane; do kubectl create namespace "$ns" --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f - kubectl create configmap cluster-gateway-ca --from-literal=ca.crt="$CA" \ -n "$ns" --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f - done ``` **Symptom if you skip it:** the agent pod sits in `ContainerCreating` with a `MountVolume.SetUp failed ... configmap "cluster-gateway-ca" not found` event. Not a crashloop, and nothing in the OpenChoreo logs mentions it. Redo it if the control plane's `cluster-gateway-ca` Certificate is ever reissued — the ConfigMap is a copy, not a reference, and nothing re-syncs it. *Registration*, by contrast, **is** declarative: the v1.2.1 CRDs accept `clientCA.secretKeyRef` with a cross-namespace `namespace`, so `registration/` references each plane's CA instead of inlining PEM the way upstream's installer does. That is why there is one bootstrap step here and not four. ## Credentials > 🔴 **`thunder/values.yaml` and `openbao/values.yaml` carry real credential > values. They are the only two files in this repo that do, and that is a > deliberate, bounded exception to the repo's sanitization rule.** They are OpenChoreo's **upstream fixture credentials** — published in `github.com/openchoreo/openchoreo`, identical in every k3d quickstart (`backstage-portal-secret`, `openchoreo-rca-agent-secret`, `ThisIsTheOpenSearchPassword1`, …). Committing them leaks nothing that is not already public. They are still real confidential-client secrets for *this* deployment. What makes that acceptable here and nowhere else: **all five OpenChoreo hostnames are public DNS records resolving to 192.168.7.150, a LAN address.** None of it is reachable from the internet — the same pattern every other `ash4d.com` service in this repo uses. Why they are literals rather than `secretKeyRef`s: each value must byte-match on both sides of an OIDC handshake, and Thunder's half lives inside a 34 KB bootstrap shell script in its own values file. Parameterising one side without the other moves the problem rather than solving it. ### Rotating the fixture credentials Do this before exposing any of these hostnames beyond the LAN. Each value must change in **both** files or the handshake breaks: | Value | `thunder/values.yaml` | `openbao/values.yaml` | |---|---|---| | Backstage OIDC | `openchoreo-backstage-client` `client_secret` | `secret/backstage-client-secret` | | Observer OIDC | `openchoreo-observer-resource-reader-client` | `secret/observer-oauth-client-secret` | | RCA agent | `openchoreo-rca-agent` | `secret/rca-oauth-client-secret` | | FinOps agent | `openchoreo-finops-agent` | `secret/finops-agent-oauth-client-secret` | | Backstage session | — | `secret/backstage-backend-secret` | Then restart OpenBao (dev mode reseeds on start) and delete the ExternalSecrets so they re-resolve immediately rather than at the 1 h refresh. **The OpenSearch password is the exception — it is write-once.** OpenSearch seeds its security index from `OPENSEARCH_INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD` on *first start only*. Changing it in `openbao/values.yaml` rotates what every client presents but not what OpenSearch accepts, leaving a cluster nothing can log into. Rotating it properly means an OpenSearch-side password change, or deleting its PVC and reindexing. ## What does not survive a restart This deployment deliberately runs three components without persistence. Knowing which is which matters more here than in any other bundle: | Component | Storage | Lost on restart | Consequence | |---|---|---|---| | **OpenBao** | none (dev mode) | everything not in `values.yaml` | ⚠️ **secrets you create through the OpenChoreo UI are gone.** Fixtures reseed automatically | | **Thunder** | in-pod SQLite | users/clients you add by hand | fixture users and OIDC clients are recreated by its bootstrap Job | | **Backstage** | in-pod SQLite | catalog cache | none — rebuilt from the API within 300 s | | OpenSearch | 8Gi Longhorn | — | persists | | Prometheus | 6Gi Longhorn | — | persists (3 d retention) | | registry | 20Gi Longhorn | — | persists | OpenBao in dev mode is the deliberate trade documented in `openbao/values.yaml`: file storage persists but **seals on every restart**, and there is no auto-unseal without a KMS. On an unattended single-node lab, "reseeds itself" beats "persists but needs a human to type unseal keys before the portal works again". **Do not use this deployment's secret management for anything you cannot recreate.** ## Resource footprint sdf1 was at **74% memory (48 GiB of 64 GiB)** and ~50% CPU requests when this was written, already running ollama on the V100, milvus, emby and the k3s control plane. Rough budget for the full stack: | Group | Memory | |---|---| | Prereqs (ESO, OpenBao, kgateway) | ~0.5 GiB | | Control plane + Thunder | ~1.5 GiB | | Data + workflow planes (idle) | ~0.5 GiB | | Observability plane + observer | ~0.5 GiB | | **OpenSearch** | **~2 GiB** | | **Prometheus** (path 19) | **~1–2 GiB** | **Enable paths 16–19 one at a time and check `kubectl top node` between each.** If it gets tight, drop in this order: `observability-metrics` (Rancher's Prometheus already covers the cluster; you lose one portal tab), then `observability-traces` (collects nothing until something is instrumented). `workflow-plane` is the one bundle that can destabilise the node *dynamically* — builds are transient and CPU-hungry, and nothing pins them away from the GPU workloads. Its `parallelism: 2` is the guardrail; cut it to 1 first. ## What is deliberately not here - **Gateway API CRDs** — k3s owns them. See Prerequisites. - **Sample workflow templates.** Upstream's installer also applies four `WorkflowTemplate`s from `samples/getting-started/`, two of which (`publish-image-k3d`, `generate-workload-k3d`) hardcode a k3d registry address. They are sample content, not cluster state — the repo's rule is that lab-fleet holds cluster state. **Consequence: builds have no template to run until you apply the non-k3d pair by hand or write your own** against `workflow-registry`. - **`samples/getting-started/all.yaml`** — the demo Projects and Components, plus `kubectl label namespace default openchoreo.dev/control-plane=true`. Labelling `default` as an OpenChoreo namespace on a cluster this busy is not something to do from a bundle. - **Harbor as the build registry.** The cluster already runs one at `registry.ash4d.com`, and it would be the better long-term target — but Harbor is deliberately outside lab-fleet (FLEET-WIRING.md: no release Secret, unreconstructable), and pointing builds at it changes the retention behaviour of a registry the `ai` namespace depends on. See `workflow-registry/fleet.yaml`. - **The Argo Workflows UI** — upstream exposes it on a LoadBalancer with `authModes: [server]`, i.e. no authentication. Dropped. - **The RCA and FinOps AI agents** — ~3 GiB between them and both need an LLM endpoint. Their credentials and Thunder clients are already seeded, so enabling either is a values change plus a model. `ollama-exporter.ai.svc:9401` is the obvious candidate, which would pull the V100 into serving them. ## Verify ```bash # Fleet state lives on the controller, not on sdf1 kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default get gitrepo lab-openchoreo \ -o jsonpath='{.status.display.state}|{.status.display.readyBundleDeployments}{"\n"}' # Are the planes registered? This is the end-to-end check — # it exercises the agents, the mTLS, the CA copy and the registration CRs. kubectl get clusterdataplane,clusterworkflowplane,clusterobservabilityplane # Agents connected? kubectl get pods -A -l app.kubernetes.io/component=cluster-agent # Certificates issued (5 across 3 namespaces) kubectl get certificate -A | grep -E 'openchoreo|observer' # Portal curl -sI https://openchoreo.ash4d.com | head -1 ``` **Traefik returning 503 for these hosts is the expected intermediate state** while a plane's chart has not yet been deployed: the `gateway-default` Service each Ingress points at is provisioned by kgateway at runtime, not by any chart here, so it does not exist until that plane is up. ## Rollback The repo-wide rule applies with extra force, because three bundles here own cluster-scoped CRDs (`external-secrets`, `kgateway-crds`, `control-plane`): > **Removing a path from `spec.paths` does not roll back — it uninstalls.** > For `control-plane` that means the 36 OpenChoreo CRDs and every Project, > Component and Workload in the cluster. Use `spec.paused: true` on the GitRepo to stop Fleet acting, and fix forward. The one safe exception is `observability-metrics`: it is a fresh release Fleet created itself with no adopted state, and its `fleet.yaml` explicitly tells you to remove it if it disturbs Rancher's monitoring.

# Fleet GitRepo — OpenChoreo.
#
# This is the Fleet `GitRepo` CUSTOM RESOURCE (gitrepos.fleet.cattle.io), not a
# git repository: it points Fleet at the existing lab-fleet repo and tells it
# which paths to render. It lives on the RANCHER CONTROLLER
# (192.168.7.148, kubectl context `rancher`), so it is not part of any bundle here.
#
#   kubectl --context rancher apply -f 14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-openchoreo.yaml
#
# ─── This one breaks the lab-<namespace> convention, deliberately ────────────
# Every other GitRepo here owns exactly one namespace. OpenChoreo spans SEVEN
# (openchoreo-control-plane, -data-plane, -workflow-plane, -observability-plane,
# thunder, openbao, external-secrets) and they are not independently useful: a
# data plane with no control plane is nothing, and the planes register with
# each other over mTLS. Splitting them into seven GitRepos would give seven
# knobs that must always be turned together, and would scatter one product's
# rollout across seven files.
#
# So this is one GitRepo per PRODUCT, staged by `spec.paths` — the same
# mechanism `lab-ai` uses, for the same reason.
#
# ─── 🔴 THIS FILE IS STAGE 1 ONLY. RE-APPLYING IT LATER RESETS spec.paths ────
# `paths` below holds the FIRST path only. The remaining nineteen are patched
# in one at a time (see gitrepos/README.md and 22-openchoreo/README.md).
#
# That means: once you have widened the live GitRepo, DO NOT `kubectl apply -f`
# this file again — it will narrow `spec.paths` straight back to one entry.
# FLEET-WIRING.md records this exact mistake being made on lab-lab-memory on
# 2026-07-30, where re-applying a GitRepo file to add `pollingInterval` silently
# reverted a hand-narrowed `spec.paths` and restarted a failing retry loop.
#
# Narrowing is not a rollback either. For `22-openchoreo/control-plane` in
# particular, removing the path uninstalls the release and takes 36 CRDs and
# every OpenChoreo object in the cluster with it. Use `spec.paused: true`.
#
# ─── Fresh install, not an adoption ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Unlike almost everything else in this repo, none of these paths adopts an
# existing release — nothing OpenChoreo-related was on the cluster beforehand.
# So the SSA field-ownership pre-flight in FLEET-WIRING.md does not apply here:
# there is no `helm` field manager to hand over from. What replaces it is
# ordering and prerequisites, which are strict. Read 22-openchoreo/README.md
# before the first apply — in particular the cluster-gateway CA bootstrap,
# which is the one step Fleet cannot do.
apiVersion: fleet.cattle.io/v1alpha1
kind: GitRepo
metadata:
  name: lab-openchoreo
  namespace: fleet-default
spec:
  repo: https://github.com/darthzen/lab-fleet
  branch: main
  # Explicit polling interval. Fleet's default is 15s, but this cluster's
  # gitjob runs with `gitjob.syncPeriod: 2h` (a Rancher fleet-chart value), and
  # on 2026-07-30 four GitRepos went dormant for 28+ minutes after a single
  # transient `context deadline exceeded` against github.com -- they only
  # recovered when an external write forced a reconcile. Stating the interval
  # here bounds how stale a repo can get and makes the intent reviewable in git
  # rather than depending on a controller-wide default. See FLEET-WIRING.md.
  pollingInterval: 60s
  paths:
    # STAGE 1 ONLY — the other nineteen are patched in one at a time.
    # NOTE `22-openchoreo` itself must NEVER appear in this list: a nested
    # fleet.yaml deploys as soon as its parent path is adopted, so adding the
    # parent would deploy all twenty bundles at once.
    - 22-openchoreo/external-secrets
  # `ash4d-lab` is a bespoke label already on the sdf1 cluster (c-nnzn9). Chosen
  # over management.cattle.io/cluster-name, which Rancher owns and may rewrite.
  # Do NOT reuse site=ash4d — that belonged to a deleted junk cluster.
  targets:
    - clusterSelector:
        matchLabels:
          ash4d-lab: ""
  # correctDrift OFF, and here it matters more than usual: OpenChoreo's own
  # controllers write to objects in these namespaces as part of normal
  # operation. Turning this on before understanding which of those writes Fleet
  # would consider drift is how you get a controller and Fleet fighting over
  # the same object. Leave it off.
  correctDrift:
    enabled: false

## `lab-openchoreo` owns seven namespaces, on purpose

It is the one exception to `lab-<namespace>`. OpenChoreo spans
`openchoreo-control-plane`, `-data-plane`, `-workflow-plane`,
`-observability-plane`, `thunder`, `openbao` and `external-secrets`, and those
are not independently useful — the planes register with each other over mTLS
and a data plane without a control plane is nothing. Seven GitRepos would mean
seven knobs that must always move together.

Two things make it unlike every other entry in the table:

- **Nothing is being adopted.** No OpenChoreo release existed on the cluster
  first, so the SSA field-ownership pre-flight in `FLEET-WIRING.md` does not
  apply — there is no `helm` field manager to hand over from. Each path
  *deploys* the moment it lands. What replaces the pre-flight is ordering, and
  it is strict.
- **One step Fleet cannot do.** The control plane's cluster-gateway CA has to
  be copied into the other three plane namespaces by hand, because it does not
  exist until the control plane has run. Skip it and three agent pods sit in
  `ContainerCreating`.

Its file, like `lab-ai`'s staging commands, holds **stage 1 only** —
`22-openchoreo/external-secrets`. Widen with `kubectl patch`, one path at a
time, in the order in `22-openchoreo/README.md`. **Do not re-apply
`lab-openchoreo.yaml` after widening**: it resets `spec.paths` back to one
entry, which is the same trap that restarted a failing loop on
`lab-lab-memory` on 2026-07-30.

`22-openchoreo` itself must never appear in `spec.paths` — a nested
`fleet.yaml` deploys as soon as its parent does, so the parent path would
deploy all twenty bundles at once.

`2026-07-30` — added, **not yet enabled**. 20 Fleet paths across seven

  useful — the planes register with each other over mTLS. Staged by

  `kubectl apply` exactly that version; doing so would be `03-gpu/runtimeclass`
  again, with every Ingress in the cluster downstream. **Same class of finding
  as the RuntimeClass one: check who owns a cluster-scoped CRD before shipping
  it, even when the version matches.**
- **A second kube-prometheus-stack is a real collision.** The OpenChoreo
  metrics module bundles one with `crds.enabled: true`, and this cluster
  already runs `rancher-monitoring` whose operator watches all namespaces.
  Resolved by disabling the bundled CRDs *and* operator and letting Rancher's
  reconcile OpenChoreo's `Prometheus`/`Alertmanager` objects — one operator,
