  path is enabled last and is explicitly droppable.
- **Not every "imperative" install step actually is.** Upstream's installer
  shells out for each plane's agent CA and inlines the PEM into the
  registration CRs, which cannot be committed. The v1.2.1 CRDs also accept
  `clientCA.secretKeyRef` with a cross-namespace `namespace`, so registration
  became an ordinary Fleet path. **Read the CRD schema before concluding
  something has to be a manual step** — one of the two apparent bootstrap
  steps here evaporated, and the other (copying the cluster-gateway CA into a
  ConfigMap per namespace) genuinely did not.
- **This cluster has TWO default StorageClasses.** `local-path` and `longhorn`
  are both annotated `is-default-class: true`, so an unset `storageClassName`
  is ambiguous, not defaulted. Every PVC in `22-openchoreo` names `longhorn`
  explicitly. Worth fixing cluster-wide, separately.
- **The repo's no-secrets rule got its first deliberate exception.**
  `22-openchoreo/thunder/values.yaml` and `openbao/values.yaml` commit

  byte-match on both sides of an OIDC handshake and Thunder's half lives inside

Done. OpenChoreo v1.2.1 is built as `22-openchoreo/` — 20 Fleet paths, 13 pinned Helm charts, 7 namespaces — plus a `lab-openchoreo` GitRepo.

**Everything is validated, nothing is deployed.** All 13 charts `helm template` clean against their pinned versions with these values, and the 4 hand-written custom resources validate against the real v1.2.1 / kgateway v2.3.1 CRD schemas.

## Three things I found that changed the design

**Gateway API CRDs are already there — owned by k3s.** `traefik-crd` in `kube-system` owns v1.5.1 standard channel with `resource-policy: keep`, which is exactly what OpenChoreo wants. Upstream's install step would have aimed Fleet at k3s's own objects — the `03-gpu/runtimeclass` failure mode with every Ingress downstream. The bundle deliberately ships none.

**The metrics module collides with Rancher's monitoring.** It bundles kube-prometheus-stack with `crds.enabled: true`, and `rancher-monitoring` already owns those ten CRDs with an operator watching all namespaces. I disabled the bundled CRDs *and* operator and let Rancher's reconcile OpenChoreo's `Prometheus`/`Alertmanager` — verified: 0 CRDs, 0 operator, correct ClusterIP:9091 service name the adapter hardcodes. A v0.87.1-vs-v0.88.1 skew remains, so that path is last and explicitly droppable.

**One "imperative" step wasn't.** Upstream shells out for each plane's agent CA and inlines PEM into the registration CRs. The CRDs also accept `clientCA.secretKeyRef` cross-namespace — so registration is an ordinary Fleet path. The other one is real: the cluster-gateway CA must be copied into three namespaces by hand once, documented with the exact command.

## Following your DNS note

Since the records point at Traefik, the kgateway Gateways are ClusterIP behind it (`kgateway-params/`) rather than taking three MetalLB IPs — you had five free. `openchoreo.ash4d.com`, `api.openchoreo.ash4d.com` and `thunder.ash4d.com` all resolve correctly.

**Two records still needed** (both NXDOMAIN): `observer.openchoreo.ash4d.com` (Backstage's telemetry tabs call it from the browser) and `*.openchoreoapis.ash4d.com` (deployed workloads). Paths 1–10 work without either.

## Two caveats worth your judgment

**I committed credential values in `thunder/values.yaml` and `openbao/values.yaml`** — a deliberate exception to this repo's sanitization rule. They're OpenChoreo's *published* upstream fixtures, and each must byte-match across an OIDC handshake where Thunder's half lives in a 34 KB bootstrap script, so `secretKeyRef` would move the problem rather than solve it. Bounded by all five hostnames resolving to a LAN address. Rotation table is in the README. If you'd rather not have them in git at all, say so — it means templating Thunder's bootstrap, which is real work but doable.

**OpenBao runs in dev mode (in-memory).** File storage persists but seals on every restart with no auto-unseal, so unattended it'd mean the portal silently losing credentials until someone types unseal keys. The cost: secrets created through OpenChoreo's UI don't survive a restart. Flagged in three places.

| `thunder` | `thunder-deployment` |

| `openchoreo-workflow-plane` | `argo-workflow-controller`, `cluster-agent-workflowplane`, `registry` |

### DNS — satisfied, verified 2026-07-30

All five hostnames resolve to **192.168.7.150** (Traefik):

```
openchoreo.ash4d.com            A   192.168.7.150   # portal
api.openchoreo.ash4d.com        A   192.168.7.150   # API / CLI
thunder.ash4d.com               A   192.168.7.150   # OIDC
observer.openchoreo.ash4d.com   A   192.168.7.150   # covered by the wildcard
*.openchoreo.ash4d.com          A   192.168.7.150   # wildcard
```

**The wildcard answers at arbitrary depth**, not just one label —
`q.r.openchoreo.ash4d.com` and `q.apps.openchoreo.ash4d.com` both resolve.
That is why deployed components live at `*.apps.openchoreo.ash4d.com` and need
no record of their own.

The nested `apps.` label is a deliberate choice, not cosmetics: the wildcard
would serve `<component>.openchoreo.ash4d.com` just as well, but then a
developer naming a component `api` or `observer` would mint a hostname that
collides with the control plane's, and which Ingress Traefik picks is
undefined. **Nobody should be able to shadow the control plane by choosing a
component name.**

An earlier draft of this bundle used a separate `*.openchoreoapis.ash4d.com`
zone for workloads. It was dropped once the existing wildcard turned out to
cover the need — one fewer DNS record to maintain.

**No hand-created Secrets.** Unlike every other bundle in this repo, there is
nothing to `kubectl create secret` — OpenBao seeds itself and ESO materialises
the rest. See "Credentials" below for the tradeoff that buys.

git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
Add 22-openchoreo: OpenChoreo v1.2.1 IDP as 20 Fleet paths

First bundle in the repo that is a platform rather than an application:
the control, data, workflow and observability planes, plus kgateway,
External Secrets, OpenBao and the Thunder OIDC provider, across seven
namespaces. Fresh install, not an adoption -- nothing OpenChoreo-related
existed on the cluster, so each path deploys the moment it lands.

Not enabled. lab-openchoreo.yaml carries stage 1 only; the remaining
nineteen paths are patched in one at a time per 22-openchoreo/README.md.

Three cluster-specific findings drove the design:

- Gateway API v1.5.1 CRDs are already present and owned by the k3s
  `traefik-crd` release with resource-policy: keep. Upstream's installer
  applies exactly that version; doing so would aim Fleet at k3s's own
  cluster-scoped objects -- the 03-gpu/runtimeclass failure mode with
  every Ingress downstream. The bundle deliberately ships none.

- The OpenChoreo metrics module bundles kube-prometheus-stack with
  crds.enabled, and this cluster already runs rancher-monitoring whose
  operator watches all namespaces. Resolved by disabling the bundled CRDs
  and operator and letting Rancher's reconcile OpenChoreo's Prometheus and
  Alertmanager -- one operator, two instances. Verified in the render: 0
  CRDs, 0 operator, service still openchoreo-observability-prometheus:9091
  as the adapter hardcodes. Leaves a v0.87.1/v0.88.1 skew, so that path is
  enabled last and is explicitly droppable.

- Upstream builds the plane-registration CRs imperatively, shelling out
  for each agent CA and inlining PEM. The v1.2.1 CRDs also accept
  clientCA.secretKeyRef with a cross-namespace namespace, so registration
  is an ordinary Fleet path. Only one genuine bootstrap step survives:
  copying the control plane's cluster-gateway CA into a ConfigMap per
  plane namespace, which cannot exist until the control plane has run.

Ingress deviates from upstream throughout: every ash4d.com name already
points at Traefik, so the three kgateway Gateways are forced to ClusterIP
via a class-wide GatewayParameters and fronted by Traefik, rather than
taking three of MetalLB's five free addresses. Deployed components sit at
*.apps.openchoreo.ash4d.com -- the nested label keeps developer-chosen
component names from shadowing api./observer. on the control plane.

thunder/values.yaml and openbao/values.yaml commit OpenChoreo's published
upstream fixture credentials. This is a bounded, deliberate exception to
the repo's no-secrets rule: each value must byte-match across an OIDC
handshake and Thunder's half lives inside a 34 KB bootstrap script, so
parameterising one side moves the problem rather than solving it. All five
hostnames resolve to 192.168.7.150, a LAN address. Rotation table is in
the README. Not a precedent -- every other secret here stays an
out-of-band prerequisite.

OpenBao runs in dev mode (in-memory) on purpose: file storage persists but
seals on every restart with no auto-unseal, which unattended means the
portal silently losing credentials. Cost: secrets created through the
OpenChoreo UI do not survive a restart. Flagged in three places.

Verified: all 13 charts helm template clean against their pinned versions
with these values, and the four hand-written custom resources validate
against the real v1.2.1 and kgateway v2.3.1 CRD JSON schemas.
